text: COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS TOWN OF HULL Annual Town Meeting Monday, May 4, 2026 at 7:00 o’clock PM At the Hull High School situated at 180 Main Street, Hull, MA PLEASE BRING THIS DOCUMENT WITH YOU TO TOWN MEETING MODERATOR’S MESSAGE HULL ANNUAL TOWN MEETING MONDAY MAY 4, 2026, 7:00 p.m. HULL HIGH SCHOOL GYMNASIUM If you are a registered voter in Hull, I urge you to attend the Town Meeting and make your voice heard as we gather to decide the future direction of the town of Hull. The warrant you have received describes the Articles that will be discussed and voted on at Town Meeting. The actual vote will be on the motion presented at the Town Meeting and the motion is not necessarily the same as the article in the warrant. However, the motion must basically adhere in scope to the article presented in the warranty or it will be ruled out of order. Please take the time to review the warrant prior to Town Meeting, doing so will allow you to have a better understanding of the issue that will come before you at Town Meeting. One of the major items considered at each year’s Town Meeting is the annual budget and Town Meeting has the right to propose changes to the budget and any warrant article by offering amendments to any motion presented. A significant amount of work is done by Town departments and volunteer committees in preparing warrant articles. These articles and all budget requests are then forwarded to the Advisory Board who then spend two to three months reviewing the budgets department by department and all articles that come before Town Meeting. All department heads appear before the Advisory Board to explain and justify their budget requests once again. Things like zoning changes and Community Preservation Committee requests also come before the Advisory Board. Finally, the Advisory Board votes on each warrant article and makes a recommendation for your consideration at Town Meeting. However, the final decision rests with you, the citizens of Hull. Key items for consideration at this year’s Town Meeting include approval of the FY26 Operating Budget of $56,615,285.The town is proposing a number of capital projects to address needed facilities and infrastructure improvements. The Community Preservation Committee is proposing funding for renovations at the Carousel, Lifesaving Museum, Village Park Playground, Hull Community Garden, funding for the Hull Community Housing Trust and preservation of historic records, among others. A number of zoning bylaw changes are being proposed by the Planning Board for Town Meeting approval. Ten citizen petitions have also been filed this year covering a number of different areas. The eleven articles proposed as part of the Consent Agenda that follows this message. Articles on the Consent Agenda are done as a single vote without presentations or debate. At the request of seven or more Town Meeting members any article can be removed from the Consent Agenda and returned to the normal order of business. The rules at Town Meeting are straightforward and are geared to provide you with the opportunity to speak and vote on each of the motions presented at Town Meeting. The detailed procedure for running Town Meeting can be found in Town Meeting Times and a link to the Citizens Guide to Town Meeting can be found at the following link: https://www.town.hull.ma.us/sites/g/files/vyhlif3286/f/uploads/citizens_guide_to_town_meeting.pdf I will briefly explain the rules at the beginning of Town Meeting. I hope you will all take the opportunity to review the Warrant prior to Town Meeting and join me at the Annual Town Meeting at Hull High School on Monday, May 4, 2026, beginning at 7 p.m. George Boylen, /s/ George Boylen, Hull Town Moderator 2026 HULL ANNUAL TOWN MEETING PROPOSED CONSENT AGENDA ARTICLE 1: Acceptance of reports. Standard housekeeping article. ARTICLE 2: Accept Liability for work performed by the Massachusetts Department of Public Works and/or Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection. Standard housekeeping article. ARTICLE 3: Authorizes Select Board/Town Manager to enter into contracts with the Massachusetts Department of Public Works and/or Commissioner and/or Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection. Standard housing keeping article. ARTICLE 4: Authorizes Select Board to enter into contracts with the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and its divisions, commissions, and agencies, including the Department of Public Works and/or County Commissioners for work related to the construction and maintenance of public highways. Standard housekeeping article. ARTICLE 5: Authorizes Treasurer/Collector to enter into compensating balance agreements per G.L. c. 44, §53F. Standard housekeeping article. ARTICLE 6: Authorizes that all income from the sale of electricity and related items be appropriated to the Hull Municipal Light Plant for its operation for the next fiscal year. Standard housekeeping article. ARTICLE 9: Funds the operation of the Harbormaster’s Department as an enterprise fund in the amount of $379,048. Standard housekeeping article. ARTICLE 10: Funds the operation of the Sewer Department as an enterprise account in the amount of $7,170,398. Standard housekeeping article. ARTICLE 11: Funds the operation of the Cable Television Public, Educational and Governmental Access Fund as an enterprise account in the amount of $332,011. Standard housekeeping article. ARTICLE 12: Authorizes an additional yearly compensation of 10% of salary but not to exceed $1,000 in accordance with G.L. c. 59, §21A to the Assessor/Assistant Assessor for successfully completing all requirements to become a certified Municipal Massachusetts Assessor or Certified Assessment Evaluator. ARTICLE 14: Allows the town to increase the maximum base amount the Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) for retirees is calculated from $20,000 annually to $21,000 annually. TOWN OF HULL Advisory Board 253 Atlantic Avenue Hull, Massachusetts 02045 781-925-2000 To the Citizens of Hull, Starting with the 2024 Town Meeting we have used a “Consent Agenda” in Town Meeting. The Consent Agenda allows the Moderator, in consultation with the Chair of the Select Board and the Chair of the Advisory Board, to combine Articles that are deemed “not likely to be controversial and not likely to generate debate” into one motion that can be passed with a simple majority. Seven or more voters in attendance may hold or remove an item from the Consent Agenda(s), to be acted on in the normal manner. The remaining Articles in the Consent Agenda will then be voted on as one motion without presentation or debate. You will see housekeeping Articles, and some of the Enterprise Fund Authorizations. These are standard Articles that we must pass each year. This Warrant contains a Projected Revenue and Expenditure Summary for the Fiscal Year ending June 30, 2027. This Summary reflects a balanced budget achieved by diligent work of all Town Departments. This enables the Town to maintain services. As has been mentioned in previous years, we look for all Town Departments to work within a budget and manage accordingly. This will be the seventh (7th) year that the Community Preservation Committee presents projects for appropriation of funds derived via the Community Preservation Act adopted by the Town. Please review these Articles and read through the Advisory Board recommendations to assist in your understanding of the Warrant. Many of the abstentions in our recommendations reflect absences of individual Advisory Board members during the applicable hearing. The Advisory Board would like to acknowledge and express our gratitude for the assistance and support of Town Manager, Jennifer Constable, Assistant Town Manager, Stacia Callahan, Administrative Assistant, Michelle LeBlanc, Town Accountant, Mike Buckley, Town Counsel, Brian Winner, and Town Clerk, Lori West. Their support allows the Advisory Board to represent and serve the Citizens of the Town of Hull at the highest level. The Advisory Board further acknowledges the work of all Department Heads, the Select Board, the School Department, Community Preservation Committee, Planning Board, Zoning By-Law Committee and the numerous other Town Boards and Commissions who have worked with the Advisory Board. The collaboration of all Town Departments, boards, committees, and employees serves the Town of Hull well. We are immensely proud of their dedication. Thank you, in advance, for your involvement and participation at this important time in Hull’s history. Sincerely, Jason Frady, Chair Chad Wolfe, Vice Chair Moraiba Reyes, Clerk Expire in 2026: Robert Carney, Moraiba Reyes Expire in 2027: David Clinton, Jason Frady, Stephen Kiley, Eric Osterberg Expire in 2028: Chad Wolfe, Heather McDonnell, Robyn Healey, Matt McGonagle ADVISORY BOARD MESSAGE Under our current form of Government, the Town Manager, with the guidance of the Select Board, prepares the Town budget and presents it to the Select Board and the Advisory Board for their review. Through discussions with the Town Manager and Department Heads, the Advisory Board reviews the budgets and makes recommendations for changes. This process usually concludes with agreement between the Advisory Board and the Town Manager in terms of presenting the budget to Town Meeting. The Advisory Board considers all Articles for the purpose of making recommendations with explanatory statements. While considering each Article many questions are considered such as: Is it necessary? Can the Town afford it? Is it in the Town's best interest? Is it fair to all? Does it affect the balance of power? Is it within legal and allowable guidelines? The following section includes a facsimile of the Town Warrant. It is called a facsimile because the actual Warrant does not include the commentary and recommendations of the Advisory Board. Some confusion has been caused in the past when motions are read at Town Meeting and are differently worded than what you see here. Motions may be worded differently so long as they are worded within the scope of the printed Article. Some people think of the printed warrant as an agenda of the Town Meeting. The legal warrant is printed, signed, and posted by our Select Board. Comments are in italicized print under the ARTICLES. The RECOMMENDATION precedes the commentary of the Advisory Board. Typical recommendations are as follows: FAVORABLE ACTION - The Advisory Board is recommending a favorable vote on the Article. UNFAVORABLE ACTION - The Advisory Board is recommending an unfavorable vote on the Article. NO RECOMMENDATION - The Advisory Board does not wish to make a recommendation or there is insufficient information to support a recommendation. RECOMMENDATION AT TOWN MEETING - The Advisory Board does not wish to make a recommendation prior to reviewing additional information or waiting for another committee to hold a public hearing. NO ACTION - A no action motion or recommendation suggests that Town Meeting set aside and prevent any further action on this Article for the meeting. REFER TO STUDY–This motion refers (commits) a matter to a committee for additional investigation and report or carry out substantive action. THE ADVISORY BOARD: J. Frady, Chair C. text: TOWN OF LEXINGTON WARRANT SPECIAL TOWN MEETING 2026-1 Commonwealth of Massachusetts Middlesex, ss. To either of the Constables or Town Clerk of the Town of Lexington, in said County, Greetings: In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are directed to notify the inhabitants of the Town of Lexington qualified to vote in elections and in Town affairs to meet either at Margery Milne Battin Hall in the Cary Memorial Building, 1605 Massachusetts Avenue, Lexington, or by means of the audio/video conferencing platform described more particularly below on Monday, the ninth day of November, 2026 at 7:30pm at which time and place the following articles are to be acted upon and determined exclusively by the Town Meeting Members in accordance with Chapter 215 of the Acts of 1929, as amended, and subject to the referendum provided for by Section eight of said Chapter, as amended. Pursuant to Chapter 92 of the Acts of 2020, as amended, including without limitation by Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2023, the Town Meeting shall be held through a hybrid of in person meeting and remote participation by the means requested by the Moderator as follows: Town Meeting members will either attend the meeting in person at Margery Milne Battin Hall, or via remote participation. The meeting will be facilitated by use of: (1) the Zoom videoconferencing platform, (2) the online voting tool developed by Select Board member Joe Pato and (3) an online queuing function developed by Select Board member Joe Pato to facilitate debate. Other Town residents who wish to follow the proceedings may do so by attending the meeting in person in the areas reserved for non-Town Meeting Members, or via LexMedia at https://www.youtube.com/user/LexMediaMATV. Other residents who wish to participate in the Meeting may email the Town Clerk's Office at clerk@lexingtonma.gov and by completing the online form at www.LexingtonMA.gov/STM2026-1 . For more information, please see the Moderator's letter dated September 28, 2026 to the Select Board attached to this warrant as Attachment A. ARTICLE 1 REPORTS OF TOWN BOARDS, OFFICERS AND COMMITTEES To receive the reports of any Board or Town Officer or of any Committee of the Town; or act in any other manner in relation thereto. (Inserted by the Select Board) DESCRIPTION: This article remains open throughout Town Meeting and reports may be presented at any Town Meeting session by boards, officers, or committees. ARTICLE 2 APPROPRIATE FOR PRIOR YEARS’ UNPAID BILLS To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate money to pay any unpaid bills rendered to the Town for prior years; to determine whether the money shall be provided by the tax levy, by transfer from available funds, or by any combination of these methods; or act in any other manner in relation thereto. (Inserted by the Select Board) FUNDS REQUESTED: Unknown at press time DESCRIPTION: This is a routine article to request funds to pay bills after the close of the fiscal year in which the goods were received or the services performed and for which no money was encumbered. 1 ARTICLE 3 ESTABLISH, AMEND, DISSOLVE AND APPROPRIATE TO AND FROM SPECIFIED STABILIZATION FUNDS To see if the Town will vote to create, amend, dissolve, rename and/or appropriate sums of money to and from Stabilization Funds in accordance with Massachusetts General Laws, Section 5B of Chapter 40 for the purposes of: (a) Section 135 Zoning By-Law; (b) Traffic Mitigation; (c) Transportation Demand Management/Public Transportation; (d) Special Education; (e) Center Improvement District; (f) Transportation Management Overlay District; (g) Capital; (h) Payment in Lieu of Parking; (i) Visitors Center Capital Stabilization Fund; (j) Water System Capital Stabilization Fund; and (k) Ambulance Stabilization Fund; determine whether such sums shall be provided by the tax levy, by transfer from available funds, from fees, charges or gifts or by any combination of these methods; or act in any other manner in relation thereto. (Inserted by the Select Board) FUNDS REQUESTED: Unknown at press time DESCRIPTION: This is an annual article to establish, dissolve, and/or fund Stabilization Funds for specific purposes and to appropriate funds therefrom. Money in those funds may be invested and the interest may then become a part of the particular fund. These funds may later be appropriated for the specific designated purpose by a two-thirds vote of an Annual or Special Town Meeting, for any lawful purpose. ARTICLE 4 AMEND FY2027 OPERATING, ENTERPRISE AND CPA BUDGETS To see if the Town will vote to make supplementary appropriations, to be used in conjunction with money appropriated under Articles 4, 5, 9 and 10 of the warrant for the 2026 Annual Town Meeting to be used during the current fiscal year, or make any other adjustments to the current fiscal year budgets and appropriations that may be necessary; to determine whether the money shall be provided by tax levy, by transfer from available funds including the Community Preservation Fund, or by combination of any of these methods; or act in any other manner in relation thereto. (Inserted by the Select Board) FUNDS REQUESTED: Unknown at press time DESCRIPTION: This is an annual article to permit adjustments to current fiscal year (FY2027) appropriations. ARTICLE 5 APPROPRIATE FOR AUTHORIZED CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS To see if the Town will vote to make supplementary appropriations to be used in conjunction with sums appropriated in prior years for the installation or construction of water mains, sewers and sewerage systems, drains, streets, buildings, recreational facilities or other capital improvements and equipment; determine whether the sums shall be provided by the tax levy, by transfer from the balances in other articles, by transfer from available funds, including enterprise funds and the Community Preservation Fund, by borrowing, or by any combination of these methods; or act in any other manner in relation thereto. (Inserted by the Select Board) FUNDS REQUESTED: Unknown at press time DESCRIPTION: This is an annual article to request funds to supplement existing appropriations for certain capital projects in light of revised cost estimates that exceed such appropriations. ARTICLE 6 ESTABLISH, AMEND AND CONTINUE DEPARTMENTAL REVOLVING FUNDS To see if the Town will vote, pursuant to the Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 44, Section 53E½ and Chapter 110 of the Code of the Town of Lexington, to amend existing revolving funds; to amend said Chapter 110 to establish new revolving funds; to determine whether the maximum amounts that may be expended from such new and existing revolving fund accounts in FY2027 shall be the following amounts or any other amounts; or act in any other manner in relation thereto. 2 (Inserted by the Select Board) FUNDS REQUESTED: Unknown at press time DESCRIPTION: The amount that may be spent from a revolving fund established under Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 44, Section 53E½ must be approved annually by Town Meeting. The Funds are credited with the receipts received in connection with the programs supported by such funds, and expenditures may be made from the revolving fund without further appropriation. This article will make amendments to the revolving funds and spending limits approved at the 2026 Annual Town Meeting. And you are directed to serve this warrant not less than fourteen days at least before the time of said meeting, as provided in the Bylaws of the Town. text: 2026 Annual Town Meeting Warrant Report Town of Lynnfield, Massachusetts THE TOWN OF LYNNFIELD 2026 ANNUAL TOWN MEETING WARRANT Annual Town Meeting April 28, 2026 1 2026 ANNUAL TOWN MEETING WARRANT TABLE OF CONTENTS Page Lynnfield Parliamentary Procedure Refresher 3 Finance Committee Report 4 Status of Town Funds 6 WARRANT FOR ANNUAL TOWN MEETING Article 1 Reports of Town Officers and Committees 7 Article 2 Appointment of Ceremonial Officers 7 Article 3 To Fix the Compensation of Elective Officers 7 Article 4 To Transfer Money to the FY2026 Budget 8 Article 5 Bills of Prior Year 8 Article 6 Appropriation of the Fiscal 2027 Budget 8 Article 7 Appropriation of the Fiscal 2027 EMS Enterprise Fund 8 Article 8 Appropriation of the Fiscal 2027 Golf Enterprise Fund 9 Article 9 Appropriation of the Fiscal 2027 Capital Budget 9 Article 10 Appropriation/Borrowing Authorization for DPW Heavy Equipment 9 Article 11 Revolving Fund Expenditure Limits 10 Article 12 Home Rule Petition to Golf/ Recreation Trust Fund 10 Article 13 Home Rule Petition Local Meals Tax 11 Article 14 Acceptance of G.L. c.40, §22F and Bylaw Amendment re: Fees 12 Article 15 Amend General By-Law Section 143-6 12 Article 16 Amend General By-Law Section 143-11 15 Article 17 Amend General By-Law Article III of Chapter 7 17 Article 18 General By-Law Restricting Cryptocurrency Machines 18 Article 19 Citizen’s Petition 20 APPENDIX A FY27 Operating Budget APPENDIX B FY27 Capital Budget APPENDIX C Definitions of Financial Terms 2 LYNNFIELD PARLIAMENTARY PROCEDURE REFRESHER The Lynnfield Town Charter requires that Town Meeting be conducted in accordance with the latest revised edition of Robert’s Rules of Order 1. Authority Precedence: Town Charter, General Laws/state law, By-Laws, Parliamentary Rules, Custom. 2. The Commonwealth permits Towns to choose the form of Government (Open Town Meeting – Select Board form in our case) and rules with which to conduct Town Meeting. Our Lynnfield Town Charter mandates the use of the latest revised edition of Robert’s Rules of Order, which currently is the 12th Edition. 3. Town Meeting is a legislative assembly. The purpose of Town Meeting is for members to freely make decisions concerning their local government. Decorum and respect for neighbors and opposing views are essential to a fair, efficient and orderly meeting. All members have the equal right to bring up ideas, discuss them and come to a conclusion subject to the rules of the meeting. 4. The Moderator has control of the meeting, directs the discussion and maintains order. 5. All debate/questions go to, and through, the Moderator. Speakers must address their remarks to the Moderator, are encouraged to maintain a respectful and courteous tone focusing on the merits of the motion, and—especially in reference to any divergence of opinion—avoid injecting remarks of a personal nature into the debate in order to ensure an efficient and orderly meeting. 6. Speakers must be recognized by the Moderator before speaking. Speakers must stand if they are able to do so, identify themselves by name, provide their address and remain standing while speaking if they are able to do so. 7. Complex motions should be made in writing and submitted to the Moderator. You may submit your motion during Town Meeting in writing to the Clerk, or by e-mail at least 24 hours prior to Town Meeting addressed to: lynnfieldTM@lynnfieldma.gov. 8. Amendments must be germane to the main motion and within the scope of the warrant article. Amendments to amendments cannot be amended. 9. Each Speaker can speak twice on the same day on a debatable pending motion for up to 10 minutes each time; however, that Speaker cannot speak for the second time until all those wishing to speak for the first time have done so. 10. Limits on speaking can be altered by 2/3 vote of Town Meeting. 11. Points of order and mandatory reporting (Finance Committee, Planning Board, etc.) are not debatable. Questions cannot be used as debate in disguise. 12. Speakers are encouraged to reference individuals in the third person or by title (i.e., “the previous speaker”, the “Selectman”, etc.) and not by name (i.e. “Joe Jones”). 13. A “majority” motion fails when there is a tie vote – the vote must be more than 1/2. In a “supermajority” vote, where there is exactly a 2/3 to 1/3 split, the 2/3 vote prevails. 14. Reconsideration is available when later substantive information may affect a prior voted motion. In order to move for reconsideration, the person making the motion must have been on the prevailing side. An article once reconsidered may not be reconsidered again. 15. While presiding, the Moderator shall not vote unless there is a tie vote and the Moderator wants to affect the result. 16. In the absence of a quorum, Town Meeting can vote to adjourn Town Meeting to a date, time and place certain. 17. Visitors/Guests can only speak with the approval of Town Meeting. 3 FINANCE COMMITTEE REPORT The Lynnfield Finance Committee is composed of eleven volunteer members appointed by the Select Board and Town Moderator to overlapping three-year terms. The Committee’s charge is to review annual expenditure requests and make budget recommendations to the community. In doing so, we seek to provide objective analysis to ensure spending decisions reflect both the Town’s needs and long-term financial sustainability. Tom Kayola, Chair Nick Connors, Vice- Chair Gene Covino, Secretary Matt Curtis Kristen Dorsky Bill Ketelhut Tony Marino Julie Mitchell Brian Moreira Rob Nickerson Select Board Moderator Moderator Select Board Moderator Select Board Select Board Select Board Moderator Moderator June ‘27 June ‘28 June ‘27 June ‘28 June ‘27 June ‘28 June ‘27 June ‘26 June ‘27 June ‘28 After careful review, the Finance Committee recommends approval of the FY27 Contingent Operating Budget of $80,565,960, as presented by the Select Board. Our recommendation follows a transparent and collaborative process that included input from department heads, the Town Administrator, the School Superintendent, and other key stakeholders. These recommendations are based on the best information available from the professionals entrusted with delivering essential Town services. Over the past year, our analysis and discussions have led to three overarching observations for the community which are largely consistent with our prior years’ statements. Rising Structural Costs and the Likelihood of Future Overrides Based on multi-year trends in expense growth, the Finance Committee believes the Town is likely to face override budget votes more regularly in future years, absent material service reductions or meaningful new revenue sources. At present, we view FY28 as a likely override year. While prior override discussions were influenced by significant labor negotiations, underlying expense growth has also accelerated across several key non-discretionary categories, including insurance, retirement obligations, and out-of-district tuition. Although labor contracts have now been resolved, these other cost drivers are expected to continue growing at elevated levels into FY27 and beyond, absorbing much of the Town’s available budget growth. These trends are not unique to Lynnfield and have affected municipalities across Massachusetts, with 37 override votes occurring over the past two years. Looking ahead, several discrete cost increases are also anticipated, including higher trash removal expenses associated with an upcoming contract renewal, increased Fire Department costs following the expiration of a significant grant, and potential Fire Department restructuring. Absent unforeseen efficiencies or new revenue sources, these pressures will likely necessitate either service reductions or override consideration. Town forecasts released last year estimated a $625,000 shortfall in FY28. While updated multi-year projections were not released this year, the Finance Committee’s analysis suggests the potential gap has widened materially. In our view, absorbing a shortfall of this magnitude would likely result in noticeable service reductions and greatly increase the likelihood of an override necessity. 4 Collaboration and Long-Term Planning The Finance Committee recognizes and appreciates the Town’s continued efforts to pursue grant funding and identify cost-saving opportunities. However, at this time, no initiatives are expected to materially offset the pace of projected expense growth. As a result, the FY27 budget relies more heavily on enterprise fund contributions, specifically golf and EMS, which represent one of the remaining available funding sources. While the Town was historically conservative in its use of enterprise funds, the FY27 budget reduces much of that cushion. With fewer financial buffers available, proactive planning and creative problem-solving will become increasingly important. The Finance Committee encourages the Town to build on recent progress and pursue cost savings and efficiencies at greater scale and more specifically act earlier in the planning process. Strengthened coordination between Town departments and School department, along with earlier identification of grant opportunities and operational improvements, may help mitigate future financial pressures. Potential areas for continued exploration include shared IT and HR services across departments; aligning fees more closely with program and facility costs; healthcare cost containment initiatives; systematic grant pursuit; private and nonprofit contributions to Town facilities; regionalization opportunities with neighboring communities; and evaluation of new revenue sources aligned with future costs, such as trash and stormwater management fees. Continued Progress in Transparency and Governance Last year, the Finance Committee called for increased meeting frequency and earlier access to budget information to improve transparency. We are encouraged by the meaningful progress made over the past twelve months, including earlier budget discussions and improved access to key leaders. We encourage continued consistency in these efforts. In particular, the absence of updated multi-year budget projections (prepared, but unreleased) limited the Committee’s ability to evaluate the longterm impact of current-year decisions. Given the financial pressures anticipated in FY28 and beyond, and the importance of identifying larger-scale cost earlier in the planning process, updated multi-year forecasting remains one of the most important opportunities for continued improvement. Looking Ahead The Finance Committee remains committed to partnering with Town leadership to preserve Lynnfield’s high level of services while maintaining long-term fiscal responsibility. While the FY27 budget reflects thoughtful planning and collaboration, structural cost pressures are expected to persist. Continued focus on efficiency, strategic planning, and transparency will be essential as the Town navigates increasingly challenging budget environments. title: Annual Town Meeting Warrant
text: Town of Mansfield ANNUAL TOWN MEETING WARRANT April 14, 2026 Adjourned to May 5, 2026 MANSFIELD HIGH SCHOOL 250 East Street Mansfield CALL TO ORDER: 7:00 PM Town of Mansfield WARRANT FOR THE ANNUAL TOWN MEETING Tuesday, April 14, 2026 (adjourned to May 5, 2026) BRISTOL, SS: To either of the Constables of the Town of Mansfield in the County of Bristol; GREETINGS: IN THE NAME OF THE COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS, you are hereby directed to notify and warn the inhabitants of said town, qualified to vote in elections and in town affairs, to meet at the Mansfield High School Auditorium, 250 East Street, Mansfield, Mansfield, Massachusetts (Precincts One, Two, Two-A, Three, Four, Five, Six, Six-A and Seven) in said Mansfield on Tuesday, April 14, 2026, at Five o’clock in the afternoon, where and when such meeting may be adjourned until Tuesday, May 5, 2026, at Seven o’clock in the evening at the said Mansfield High School Auditorium, or some other convenient date and time, then and there to act on the following articles: Article 1: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds or borrow pursuant to any applicable statute a sum of money to defray the expenses of the Municipal Town departments for the ensuing 12-month period beginning July 1, 2026; or take any other action in relation thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board Explanation: This article (if approved) establishes the FY2027 budget appropriations for municipal expenses, as well as all debt, insurance and employee benefits for all Town and School departments. Article 2: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds or borrow pursuant to any applicable statute a sum of money to defray the expenses of the Mansfield Public School System for the ensuing 12-month period beginning July 1, 2026; or take any other action in relation thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board for Mansfield School Committee Explanation: This article (if approved) establishes the FY2027 budget appropriations for the School Department. Article 3: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds or borrow pursuant to any applicable statute a sum of money to supplement the amounts appropriated pursuant Article 1 of this warrant, to defray the expenses of the Municipal Town departments for the ensuing 12-month period beginning July 1, 2026; and to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds or borrow pursuant to any applicable statute a sum of money to supplement the amounts appropriated pursuant to Article 2 of this Warrant, to defray the expenses of the Mansfield Public School System for the ensuing 12-month period beginning July 1, 2026; provided however, such supplemental appropriations shall be contingent upon the passage of a ballot question allowing the town to assess additional real estate and personal property taxes in an amount in excess of the limitations on taxes of Proposition Two and One-Half so called (chapter 59, section 21C(g) of the General Laws), or take any other action in relation thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board Page 2 of 19 Explanation: Articles 1 and 2 allocate the town’s existing tax levy and other available revenues but at a reduced budget level. However, if approved, this article would provide supplemental funding to the FY2027 budget to ensure that municipal and school operating expenses, as well as all debt, insurance, and employee benefits for Town and School Departments, are maintained. Since the reduced budgets in Articles 1 and 2 are insufficient to sustain these service levels, this additional funding would require voter approval of an operating override at the ballot, exceeding the tax limitations set by Proposition Two and One-Half. Article 4: To see if the Town will vote that the income from sales of electricity to private customers or for electricity supplied to municipal buildings, together with receipts from jobbing accounts, be appropriated for the Municipal Electric Department, the whole to be expended by the Manager of the Municipal Electric Department under the direction and control of the Select Board acting as Electric Commissioners, for expenses of the Department for FY2026, as defined in Section 57 of Chapter 164 of the General Laws, and that, if said sum and said income shall exceed said expense for said fiscal year, such excess shall be transferred to the construction fund of said plant and appropriated and used for such additions thereto as may thereafter be authorized by the Electric Commissioners; or take any other action in relation thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board for Municipal Electric Commissioners Explanation: This article (if approved) provides the appropriation from Electric Department receipts for the Electric Department maintenance and plant operations for FY 2027. Article 5: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate from Enterprise Fund Revenue or any other source, transfer from available funds or borrow pursuant to any applicable statute a sum of money to provide for the operations, maintenance, improvements, capital outlay, debt service, and other costs related to the Water Enterprise Fund, Sewer Enterprise Fund, Airport Enterprise Fund, and Parking Enterprise Fund for the ensuing 12 month period beginning July 1, 2026; or take any other action in relation thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board Explanation: This article (if approved) will establish the FY2027 budget appropriations for the Water, Sewer, Airport, and Parking Enterprise Funds. Article 6: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds, or borrow pursuant to any applicable statute a sum of money for various Capital Improvements projects for the Town of Mansfield; or take any other action in relation thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board for Capital Improvement Program Committee Explanation: This article will contain several motions to fund the Capital Improvement Program Committee’s recommended Town, School, Sewer Enterprise, Water Enterprise, Airport Enterprise, and Parking Enterprise projects. This article (if approved) will fund the Capital Improvement Program Committee’s recommendations. Article 7: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, or transfer from available funds the sum of $349,600.00 to be expended by the Director of the Department of Public Works to fund in part the Snow and Ice Deficit, or take any other action relative thereto. Explanation: This article would appropriate funds to balance the deficit carried by the snow and ice account for snow removal services for the current fiscal year. The sum proposed to be funded by available Page 3 of 19 Certified Free Cash with the remaining deficit to be covered through Reserve Fund and interdepartmental transfers at the end of the year. Article 8: To see if the Town will vote to amend Chapter 59 of the Town’s General Bylaws, Revolving Funds, Section 52-5 as follows (additions show in bold and underline and deletions shown in strikethrough): § 52-5. Funds. SPONSOR: Select Board Explanation: This Article updates the types of revenue that may be placed in the Ambulance Revolving Fund. Article 9: To see if the Town will vote to set the annual spending limits for each of the Departmental revolving funds set forth in Mansfield Town Code Chapter 52 entitled “Revolving Funds”, or take any other action in relation thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board Explanation: The Town is required per Massachusetts General Law Chapter 53 E ½ to annually set the expenditure limits in our revolving funds. Page 4 of 19 Article 10: To see if the Town will raise and appropriate, borrow, or transfer from available funds a sum of money for deposit in the following funds: Employee Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) Liability Trust Fund; Future Payment of Accrued Liabilities for Compensated Absences Reserve Fund; Special Injury Leave Indemnity Fund; Town’s Special Education Reserve Fund; Town’s Opioid Mitigation Stabilization Fund; and/or Stabilization Fund; or take any other action in relation thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board for Finance Committee Explanation: The Town is required to pay a percentage of retirees’ medical, dental, and life insurance costs. The Town’s net OPEB liability as of FY2024 is estimated at $114 million. This article (if approved) will transfer a sum of money into the OPEB Trust Fund to offset some of those future costs This article (if approved) will deposit a sum of money into this Reserve Fund and allow the Town Manager to pay compensated absence expenses as outlined in M.G.L. Chapter 40 Section 13D. At the May 2, 2017 Annual Town Meeting, Town Meeting authorized the creation of a Special Injury Leave Indemnity Fund for payment of police officers’ or firefighters’ injury leave compensation or medical bills incurred under M.G.L. Chapter 41 Section 111F. These bills can be costly and may continue for extended periods of time. This article (if approved) will deposit a sum of money into this Indemnity Fund and allow the Town Manager to pay expenses as outlined in M.G.L. Chapter 41 Section 111F 4 th paragraph. At the May 2, 2017 Annual Town Meeting, Town Meeting authorized the creation of a Special Education Reserve Fund for payment of certain Special Education – related expenses. This article (if approved) will deposit a sum of money into this Reserve Fund and allow the Mansfield School Committee (with the approval of the Select Board) to pay Special Education – related expenses as outlined in M.G.L. Chapter 40 Section 13E. This article (if approved) will transfer a sum of money into the Town’s Stabilization Fund. It can then be used for any lawful purpose as outlined in M.G.L. Chapter 40 Section 5B. Article 11: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds, or borrow pursuant to any applicable statute a sum of money to pay for unpaid prior year’s bills; or take any action in relation thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board Explanation: In general, appropriated amounts at Town Meeting for one Fiscal Year cannot be spent on a previous year’s expenditures without Town Meeting approval. This article (if approved) would pay for these outstanding bills that are presently known to be unpaid from prior Fiscal Years. Page 5 of 19 Article 12: To see if the Town will vote to amend Chapter 81 of the General Bylaws by inserting a new Article III as follows: Article III – Fire Safety Compliance and Electronic Reporting § 81-22 Purpose. The purpose of this bylaw is to ensure timely compliance with the Massachusetts Comprehensive Fire Safety Code (527 CMR 1.00) and to facilitate efficient submission, review, and tracking of all required fire‑safety inspections, tests, certifications, and related documentation. § 81-23 Applicability. This bylaw applies to all owners of buildings, structures, and premises for which 527 CMR requires inspections, maintenance records, test reports, or other fire‑safety documentation. § 81-24 Electronic Submission Requirement. (a) All required reports, documentation, permits, certifications, inspection results, and maintenance records mandated under 527 CMR shall be submitted electronically. (b) Submissions must be made through an electronic reporting platform or compliance management system approved by the Fire Chief. (c) The Fire Chief is authorized to publish procedures, technical standards, and submission deadlines for the electronic reporting system. § 81-25 Noncriminal Disposition. The provisions of this bylaw may be enforced by noncriminal disposition, as provided in Massachusetts General Laws, Chapter 40, § 21D. The penalty for such violation shall be one hundred dollars ($100) for the first offense, two hundred dollars ($200) for the second offense, and three hundred dollars ($300) for the third and each subsequent offense. Each day during which a violation exist shall constitute a separate offense. SPONSOR: Select Board Explanation: This article asks voters if they will approve an amendment to the General Bylaw requiring that any installation, maintenance, inspection of fire suppression systems be reported to the Mansfield Fire Department, as required by Massachusetts Board of Fire Prevention Regulations 527 CMR, through such electronic reporting platform as shall be designated by the Fire Chief. Article 13: To see if the Town will vote to amend Chapter 94 Article III of the General Bylaws of the Town of Mansfield as follows: (1) By amending Section 94-19 as follows (additions shown in bold): Except as otherwise provided, no person shall erect, construct, change the use of or provide an addition of more than 20% to any building or structure or any part thereof, or cause the same to be done, which fails to support adequate radio coverage for the Town of Mansfield radio communications system, including but not limited to firefighters and police officers. All buildings and structures subject to this bylaw shall comply with the Mansfield requirements for the installation of public safety radio signal booster system specifications (the “Public Safety Radio Signal Booster Specification”), as may be jointly adopted and amended from time to time by the Fire Chief and Police Chief. Copies of the Public Page 6 of 19 Safety Radio Signal Booster Specification shall be maintained by the Fire and Police Departments and made available for public inspection at reasonable times. (2) By deleting Section 94-21 in its entirety and inserting, in place thereof, the following: A. Buildings and structures which cannot support the required level of radio coverage shall be equipped with a system compliant with the Public Safety Radio Signal Booster Specification. B. All public safety radio signal booster systems required under this bylaw shall be designed, installed, tested, and maintained in compliance with the Public Safety Radio Signal Booster Specification. (3) By deleting Section 94-22 in its entirety and inserting, in place thereof, the following: A. When an in-building radio system is required, and upon completion of the installation, it will be the building owner's responsibility to have the radio system tested to ensure that two-way coverage on each floor is compliant with the Public Safety Radio Signal Booster Specification. B. A certificate of occupancy will not be issued to any structure if the building fails to comply with this section. (4) By deleting Section 94-23 in its entirety and inserting, in place thereof, the following: A. After an in-building radio system is installed, the building owner shall be responsible for the annual testing of the system to be compliant with the Public Safety Radio Signal Booster Specification. B. Upon completion of the annual test of the system, the person performing the test shall provide the Mansfield Police/Fire Communications Center with a copy of the test results. Or take any other action relative thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board Explanation: This article eliminates detailed technical specifications currently embedded in the bylaw and instead requires compliance with a separate specification document maintained by the Fire and Police Departments. This change avoids inconsistencies between documents and allows technical standards to be updated administratively by the Fire and Police Chiefs as technology and operational needs evolve. Article 14: To see if the Town will vote to authorize the Fire Chief, on behalf of the Town and in accordance with Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 30B and any other applicable laws, to enter into a lease agreement with ZOLL Medical Corporation for the lease of cardiac monitor defibrillators and participation in the ZOLL One service program for a term not to exceed ten years, said agreement to commence in Fiscal Year 2027; and to authorize the Town Manager to execute said agreement and any related documents; with all payments to be funded through the Fire Department operating budget in Fiscal Year 2027 and in each subsequent fiscal year of the lease term; or take any other action relative thereto. SPONSOR: Select Board Explanation: This article authorizes the Fire Department to enter into a ten-year lease agreement with ZOLL Medical Corporation for cardiac monitor defibrillators and the ZOLL One service program beginning in Fiscal Year 2027. All costs will be paid through the Fire Department operating budget. Page 7 of 19 Moving to a lease model eliminates the need for large periodic capital requests to replace cardiac monitors. Instead of seeking substantial one-time appropriations every several years, the Town will pay predictable annual costs through the operating budget. The ZOLL One program also includes maintenance, service, software updates, and device replacement as needed. This ensures equipment remains current and fully supported without unexpected repair or upgrade costs. This approach provides stable budgeting, reduces financial spikes in the capital plan, and ensures frontline EMS crews have reliable, up to date cardiac monitoring equipment at all times. Article 15: To see if the Town will vote to accept the Right of Way for Cobb Street, as shown on the plan titled” Acceptance Plan for Cobb Street in Mansfield, Massachusetts” on file with the Town Clerk’s Office. This will give the Advisory Board additional time to review budget information and provide comment at a future time. 5 Moderator’s Town Meeting Rules (Revised February 2019) 1. The conduct of Marshfield’s Town Meeting is governed by Federal and State law, the Town’s Charter and By-Laws, local tradition, and the publication entitled “Town Meeting Time: A Handbook of Parliamentary Law.” 2. The Moderator shall preside and regulate the proceedings, decide all questions of order, and make public declaration of all votes. (Mass. G.L. c. 39, §15) 3. There will be no quorum required for Marshfield Town Meetings. (Bylaw Art. 1 §3) 1988ATM.art.15 4. All Special and Annual Town Meeting articles will be voted by lottery. The exception will be the operating budget articles at the beginning of the Annual Meeting. The Moderator may also propose linkage of similar articles. (Bylaw Art. 1§6) 2006ATM.art.18. The Moderator may also, with the permission of Town Meeting, utilize a consent agenda to consider and to pass without debate non-controversial warrant articles. 5. The Moderator may call for a voice vote, standing vote, show of hands, roll-call vote or secret ballot. A motion for any of these voting methods may be made at any time during the discussion phase of an article by a recognized voter. A majority of the voters must approve any motion for a roll call vote or a vote by secret ballot. If the declared results of voice votes or show of hands votes are questioned by seven (7) voters standing immediately after the declared vote, a standing vote will be taken without debate. 6. All matters shall be decided by a majority vote unless a 2/3 or greater vote is required. If more than a majority vote is required, the Moderator shall announce the required percentage for passage before calling for the vote. 7. No reconsideration of an article or vote will be permitted unless the Moderator determines that there has been a significant procedural error or that there is new information likely to have affected the previous vote. If a motion to reconsider is accepted by the Moderator, it will require a majority vote for passage. There will be no reconsideration after 10:30 p.m. on the evening of the vote in question. 8. No article may be reconsidered on a subsequent evening unless postponed by motion for that purpose, during the same session at which the article was first voted upon. (Bylaw Art. 1 §4) 9. To address Town Meeting, a speaker must first be recognized by the Moderator, then give his or her name and address for the record. All questions and comments by a speaker should be addressed to the Moderator and not to any particular town official or other Town 6 Meeting member. No speaker will be recognized while another person is speaking. No person shall address Town Meeting without leave of the Moderator, and all persons shall, at the request of the Moderator, be silent. If a person, after warning from the Moderator, persists in disorderly behavior, the Moderator may order him/her to withdraw from the meeting. If he/she does not withdraw, the Moderator may order a constable or other person to remove him/her. (Mass. G.L. c.39, §17). The sole exception to the “only one person talking at a time” rule is a “point of order” which is used to question a procedural point the Moderator may have missed. It is also used to question an action that is contrary to proper procedure or that is misleading to the Town Meeting. Points of order are NOT to address the subject matter being discussed. All points of order are decided by the Moderator alone without debate. 10. The Moderator may set time limits on all presentations. He or she may also set limits on the number of times a voter can speak on an article and for how long. The Moderator may terminate debate on a motion when he or she deems it appropriate. Debate on a motion may also be terminated by a recognized voter “moving the question” which, if accepted by the Moderator as not being premature, shall be voted on without discussion or debate. A motion to “move the question” requires a 2/3 vote for passage. 11. Articles in the Warrant give notice of the subjects to be discussed at Town Meeting and establish the parameters of matters that can be debated and acted upon. Amendments, motions, and/or debate determined by the Moderator, with the advice of Town Counsel, to be “beyond the scope” of the article, shall not be permitted. 12. Only two (2) amendments to a motion may be on the floor at any particular time. Generally, amendments shall be voted on in the order made and prior to the vote on the motion to be amended. Amendments over ten (10) words must be submitted to the Moderator in writing and, if over fifty (50) words, sufficient copies must be available at the entrance of the hall before the start of that particular session. Before an amendment to a particular article or motion can be accepted by the Moderator, a determination must first be made by the Moderator, with the assistance and upon the advice of Town Counsel, as to (a) whether the proposed amendment is within the scope of the article or motion and (b) whether the form and substance of the proposed amendment complies with the laws of the Commonwealth. For this reason, all proposed amendments should be submitted to the Moderator and to Town Counsel well in advance of the particular Town Meeting at which the proposed amendment will be introduced. 13. Differing dollar amounts to be appropriated shall be voted on in descending order, with the largest sum first, until an amount gains approval. 14. Non-voters will be seated in a special section unless permission is granted by the Town Meeting to be seated elsewhere. Non-voters may be allowed to address the Town Meeting with permission of the Moderator unless a majority of voters choose to deny such a privilege. 7 15. A resolution is a non-debatable, non-binding motion on any matter calling for a consensus of the Town Meeting. If a resolution is over ten (10) words, it must be submitted to the Moderator in writing and, if over fifty (50) words, sufficient copies must be available at the entrance of the hall to those attending. Resolutions are typically taken up as the last order of business at Town Meeting. The Board of Selectmen, within 30 days after a Town Meeting, shall discuss in open session any Resolution passed at such meeting. (Bylaw Art.51) 1980ATM.art.35 16. No new business will be taken up after 10:30 p.m. on any evening. 17. When justice or order requires, the Moderator may make exceptions to those rules as he/she, in his/her discretion, deems it appropriate under the circumstances and with the concurrence of a majority of the Town Meeting members. 8 Reminder – State Law prohibits SMOKING on school property. MUNICIPAL FINANCE TERMS APPROPRIATION – An authorization by the Town Meeting to make obligations and payments from the treasury for a specific purpose. ASSESSED VALUATION – A valuation set upon real or personal property by the Board of Assessors as a basis for levying taxes. BETTERMENT – A betterment assessment is a charge for the cost of public improvements, which benefit a limited area, against real estate situated in such. BAN – “Bond Anticipatory Note”. Short term borrowing done in advance of long-term borrowing via issuance of a BOND. BANs are issued to be able to fund a project while waiting to go to formal bonding. BOND – A loan, typically over a year in maturity. BOND AUTHORIZATION – The amount of money the Town Meeting approves for borrowing for a specific purpose. BOND / BAN PREMIUM – Funds paid to the Town by financial institutions as commissions on the sale of the Town’s BONDS or BANs. These premiums are allowed under the Massachusetts Municipal Act of 2016 under Chapter 44, section 20 to be used to fund similar Capital Projects to the projects funded by the original BOND/BAN. BOND ISSUE – Generally, the sale of a certain number of bonds at one time by a governmental unit. CAPITAL BUDGET – A plan of proposed capital outlays and the means of financing them for the current fiscal period. CAPITAL OUTLAY – An expenditure for the purchase of property or equipment and for the construction or renovation of a facility and infrastructure. CHERRY SHEET – A form showing all state and county charges and reimbursements to the town as certified by the Massachusetts Department of Revenue. DEBT SERVICE – Payment of interest and repayment of principal to holders of the town’s debt instruments. ENTERPRISE FUND – Financing of services where all or most of the costs are paid for by users. 9 ENTERPRISE RETAINED EARNINGS – If during a fiscal year an Enterprise fund produces a surplus, such surplus shall be kept in a separate account called “retained earnings”. The Department of Revenue then certifies that surplus as an available fund which can be used for: 1. operating costs to offset the need to increase user charges, 2. to fund capital improvements, 3. to reimburse General Fund to the extent the General Fund has funded a particular service in prior years, or 4. to fund Enterprise Fund revenue deficits. FISCAL YEAR - A 12-month period, commencing on July 1, to which the annual budget applies. (Abbreviated as "FY".) FREE CASH - The excess of assets over liabilities, minus uncollected taxes of prior years, also referred to as "available cash". The amount is certified annually by the Massachusetts Department of Revenue. Free Cash may be appropriated by vote of a town meeting. GENERAL FUND - The major town owned fund which is created with town receipts and which is charged with expenditures payable from such revenues. GRANT - A contribution of assets by one governmental unit or other organization to another. Typically, these contributions are made to local governments from the state and federal government. Grants are usually made for specific purposes. LEVY LIMIT - The amount of dollars a Town can raise by taxation under Proposition 2 ½. LINE-ITEM BUDGET - A format of budgeting which organizes costs by type of expenditure. Such as expenses, equipment, and salaries. OVERLAY - The overlay is the amount raised by the Assessors to be used for potential abatement of property taxes. The Overlay Surplus is the portion of each year's overlay account no longer required to cover property tax abatements. PROPERTY TAX LEVY - The amount produced by multiplying the assessed valuation of property by the tax rate. The tax rate is expressed "per thousand dollars" of assessed valuation. RESERVE FUND - Money set aside by Town Meeting to be allocated by the Advisory Board for extraordinary and unforeseen expenditures. REVOLVING FUND (Ch.44, Sec. 53E 1/2) - A Town may annually authorize the use of a revolving fund by accounting for separately the receipts received from a particular service or program and expend from such fund for providing such service or program without appropriation. STABILIZATION FUND - A special account which is invested until used and can only be utilized by town meeting appropriation. 10 TOWN OF MARSHFIELD COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS SPECIAL TOWN MEETING WARRANT Special Town Meeting, Monday, April 27, 2026 At 7:00 o’clock in the evening at the Marshfield High School Gymnasium Plymouth, SS: To either of the constables in the Town of Marshfield in the County of Plymouth. General Laws Chapter 43B, Section 10 (c) requires the Attorney General to furnish “a written opinion setting forth any conflict between the proposed amendment and the constitution and laws of the commonwealth.” We do not find any conflict with the charter amendment adopted under Article 29 and the Constitution or laws of the Commonwealth (“state law”). Our review is confined to the proposed charter amendments submitted to this Office for review and does not include a review of the existing text in the Town’s charter. However, we remind the Town to consult with Town Counsel to ensure compliance with the charter amendment procedures established under G.L. c. 43B, §§ 11 and 12, including the filing requirements for approved charter amendments in Section 12 which states in relevant part: Section 12. Certificates in quadruplicate shall be prepared setting forth any charter that has been adopted or revised and any charter amendments approved and shall be signed by the city or town clerk. DILLON Welcome to the 2026 Annual Town Meeting! Please note that, per Order of the Select Board, Town Meeting will begin on Wednesday, May 6, 2026, at 7:30 PM EST at the Milton High School auditorium. During this Annual Town Meeting, there are forty-two (42) articles for your review and consideration. Articles 1-2, 4-16, 21, 23-29, 33-35 and 37-41 were submitted by the Select Board. Article 3 was submitted by the Select Board and Capital Improvement Planning Committee. Article 17 was submitted by the Board of Health. Article 18 was submitted by the Board of Library Trustees. Article 19 was submitted by the Board of Cemetery Trustees. Article 20 was submitted by the Board of Park Commissioners. Article 22 was submitted by the School Committee. Articles 30-32 were submitted by the Community Preservation Committee. Article 36 was submitted by the Fire Station Building Committee. We will follow Rule 15 which describes the Consent Agenda, adopted at the May 7, 2018, Annual Town Meeting. A Consent Agenda will be circulated prior to this year’s Annual Town Meeting. The Warrant Committee has reviewed each article. If applicable, any Warrant Committee recommendations and comments not included in this Warrant will be available on the Town Meeting website prior to May 6, 2026, and hard copies will be provided at Town Meeting. Please carefully review each article and direct any questions to the submitting party prior to Town Meeting. Please note that, upon the advice of Town Counsel, the Warrant Committee’s recommendations have been streamlined. Specifically, where the Warrant Committee recommends the Town adopt the article as printed in the Warrant, the Warrant so states briefly. If the Warrant Committee recommends changes to the article, the changes are presented to clarify the difference to the reader. The following rules shall apply to this Town Meeting: First, Town Meeting Members are required to check in with the Town Clerk and to be seated in the lower part of the auditorium, which is demarcated and reserved for Town Meeting Members. Town citizens and others who are not Town Meeting Members are required to be seated in the upper part of the auditorium. Exceptions may be made for minor children and for any appropriate accommodation, and requests shall be made in writing in advance to the Moderator. Second, any Town Meeting Member wishing to speak to any article or pending related matter will first go to the nearest microphone and, upon being recognized by the Moderator, will identify themself by giving their name and precinct. If you have not been recognized by the Moderator, you are not permitted to speak to the meeting. On occasion members will informally alert the Moderator that they desire to be recognized to speak on a certain article. While your Moderator will attempt to remember who desires to be recognized on any article, please be advised that the only way in which a member can be sure to be recognized is to go to a 9 microphone and wait to be recognized. Note that the Moderator will not address any speaker by name until the speaker has first identified themselves. Third, by longstanding tradition, while any other voter of the Town who is not a Town Meeting Member may not, vote they may be recognized to address Town Meeting providing that the voter in advance of the particular session has obtained permission from the Moderator. Permission shall be requested no later than 5 PM EST on April 29, 2026. Permission may be granted after the deadline in the Moderator’s sole discretion. Fourth, any person having a monetary or equitable interest in, or who is employed as an attorney or otherwise by another person interested in, any matter under discussion shall disclose the fact of their interest or employment before speaking thereon. Fifth, with reference to each article in the warrant the recommendation of the Warrant Committee shall ordinarily be considered to have been presented in the form of a motion by the Chairperson which has been seconded by the Secretary or other member of the Warrant Committee who is a Town Meeting Member. Unless the Moderator otherwise expressly states at the time, the question to be voted on under each article will usually be whether to accept the recommendation of the Warrant Committee. In other words, generally the recommendation of the Warrant Committee is the main motion pending under the Article. In the event that the Warrant Committee recommends a NO vote on an article, the question will be presented as a vote on a motion made and seconded to approve the article, i.e., Members will vote YES if they favor the article and NO if they oppose the article, as recommended by the Warrant Committee. The Moderator shall clarify this point during Town Meeting. Please direct any question to the Moderator. Sixth, pursuant to Section 4 of Chapter 2 of the Town’s bylaws, the Moderator requires that all substantive or complex motions be reduced to writing and presented to the Moderator before submission to the meeting. All such motions shall be submitted by no later than 5 PM EST on April 29, 2026. Permission may be granted after the deadline in the Moderator’s sole discretion. Seventh, by longstanding tradition, “Town Meeting Time, A handbook of Parliamentary Law” 4th Edition, will, in addition to the bylaws of the town of Milton and the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, be the rules of order for this meeting. Eighth, any member desiring to show slides, make a PowerPoint presentation or any other visual material before the meeting must make appropriate arrangements and inform the Moderator. Such requests must be made by no later than 5 PM EST on April 29, 2026. Permission may be granted after the deadline in the Moderator’s sole discretion. Ninth, members are urged to obtain all information needed by them prior to the meeting. However, by tradition the Moderator will recognize any Town Meeting Member for the purpose of requesting additional information relevant to the matter under consideration. All such requests must be directed solely to the Moderator who will attempt to ascertain the most appropriate official who should answer such an inquiry. Answers will not be provided while the member still 10 has the floor to prevent the temptation to cross-examine the person providing the information, which is not permitted. However, the Moderator will separately recognize a member once for the purpose of posing a follow-up question. Sometimes the information is not available or is not immediately available and the request for information will simply not be fulfilled. Tenth, when it is announced by the Moderator that the Meeting will proceed to vote, debate will be closed and the pending question will be put to the Town Meeting. Eleventh, upon a question being put to the Town Meeting, the Moderator may first determine by voice vote the sense of the Meeting. If the Moderator is unable to decide by the sound of the voices or if her announcement of the vote is doubted by seven Town Meeting Members standing in their place, the Moderator shall then proceed to have a standing vote on the question. If the vote is further doubted by twenty-five Town Meeting Members standing in their places, then there will be a roll call of the meeting with the Town Clerk calling the name of each Town Meeting Member in alphabetical order and each Town Meeting Member upon their name being called shall rise in place and answer YES or NO. If an individual is unable to stand, they shall alert the Moderator. When an electronic voting system approved by the Moderator is in use, upon a question being put to the Town Meeting, the Moderator will determine by electronic vote the sense of the meeting and shall announce the vote as displayed by the electronic voting system. Milton routinely holds Special Town Meetings for the purpose of addressing certain articles prior to the next Annual Town Meeting. During this October Special Town Meeting, there are nine (9) articles for your review and consideration. Articles 1-3, 6-8 were submitted by the Select Board. Article 4 was submitted by the Community Preservation Committee (CPC). Article 5 was submitted by the Planning Board. Article 9 was submitted by Citizens’ Petition. The Warrant Committee has reviewed each article and has provided its comments. If applicable, any Warrant Committee comments not included in this warrant will be available on the Town Meeting website prior to October 19, 2026, and hard copies will be provided on green sheets at Town Meeting. As is customary, I will co-host a show with our Warrant Committee Chair, Jay Fundling, on Milton Access Television and available on YouTube prior to Town Meeting.
