Dillon Elizabeth Dillon, Town Moderator 7 REPORT OF THE WARRANT COMMITTEE FOR THE 2026 OCTOBER SPECIAL TOWN MEETING Greetings to the Honorable Select Board, Town Meeting members and Residents of the Town of Milton: The Warrant Committee herein presents to the Town Meeting recommendations for action on Articles submitted to the Special Town Meeting convening on Monday, October 19, 2026. There are nine articles for this Special Town Meeting. These Articles address a variety of issues that concern the Town beyond the typical zoning matters we historically address at Town Meeting. There are five articles submitted by the Select Board, one article submitted by the Planning Board, one article submitted by the Community Preservation Committee, and one article submitted by a Citizens’ Petition. The Warrant Committee has reviewed all articles and suggests the Town take action on the first eight articles, while sending the ninth back to the Select Board for study. For each article, the Warrant Committee’s recommendation in bold is the motion before Town Meeting and the place where Town Meeting will begin its discussion. Article 1 allocates additional state funds that were not expected when we approved the 2026-27 budget at the last Annual Town Meeting. This article allocates this money to the Reserve Fund. Article 2 reallocates funds borrowed for certain projects - but ultimately not needed for those projects to other projects. Article 3 authorizes the town to spend to improve water mains in coordination with other adjacent projects. These projects may be funded with 0% MWRA loans. Article 4 authorizes the CPC to fund a playground improvement at Tucker School. Article 5 clarifies the MBTA zoning to state that there be a minimum of 15% Affordable Housing in the larger developments. Articles 6 and 7 are both related to the possible purchase of the former Labouré College property located at 303 Adams Street. Article 6 is the approval of the purchase itself. This article requests Town Meeting’s approval to purchase the property at the price of $11,750,000 negotiated by the Select Board. Such purchase will then require the approval of a debt exclusion measure by the registered voters of the Town at a later date. 8 A potential plan for the town’s use of this property is to alleviate the schools’ overcrowding at a potentially more affordable cost than the current proposed project on Gile Road. Article 7 provides funding to the School Building Committee for a study to thoroughly examine the option of a school on this location and compare the two alternatives. Article 8 amends the appropriation from the PEG Access Enterprise Fund for Fiscal Year 2027. The Warrant committee supports all the above Articles, as described further in the comments below. Article 9 is a petition submitted by over 100 citizens regarding the use of surveillance technology in town. The Warrant Committee discussed this petition with the Police Chief, who noted that the way that the article is worded could have unintended negative consequences. It is our understanding that the Select Board will be examining this issue in the near future, probably before this Special Town Meeting. We recommend this issue be taken up for study by the Select Board and not voted on at this meeting. Throughout the Warrant you will see the Warrant Committee’s recommendations printed in bold. While these recommendations are an important part of the Warrant Committee’s job, they are not the most important part. More important than telling you what the Warrant Committee recommends is telling you why we recommend it. You – the legislative body of the Town, representing all Town voters – will make the ultimate decision on all of these articles. The Warrant Committee endeavors to provide you, through our written comments and our presentations before Town Meeting, the reasons why we made the decisions we did, along with enough information to make your decision on our recommendation. You may agree with some of our recommendations, and you may disagree with others. But if we have provided you with enough information to efficiently and confidently make your decision, then the Warrant Committee will consider its job done. The Chair wishes to express his appreciation to the members of the Warrant Committee for the many hours of work required to prepare this Warrant. The Warrant Committee also extends thanks to the Town Administrator, Mr. Nicholas Milano, the Select Board, the Planning Board, and all the other departments throughout the Town for their continued assistance in our mandate. The Chair is especially grateful for the assistance of the Warrant Committee Clerk, Karen Bosworth. LeeMichael McLean Nicole Boyson Rukstalis Lindsey Sands Ronald Sia Jimmy Stournaras Nicholas Tangney Cecille Yang Jay Fundling, Chair Elaine Craghead, Secretary Jamesley Dasse Lorraine Dee Lawrence Johnson Liveda Johnson Andrew Koh Macy Lee Karen Bosworth, Clerk 9 ARTICLE 1 To see by what sum of money the Town will vote to amend the appropriations voted at the 2026 Annual Town Meeting for the twelve-month period beginning July 1, 2026; and to determine how said appropriations shall be raised, whether by transfer from available funds or otherwise; and to act on anything related thereto. Submitted by the Select Board. RECOMMENDED that the Town vote to amend the following appropriation voted by the 2026 Annual Town Meeting by the article referenced in the table below, and in the manner identified below, for the twelve-month period beginning July 1, 2026: Department Reserve Fund 2026 ATM Article 27 Current FY2027 Appropriation $300,000 FY2027 Adjustment $363,469 Revised FY2027 Appropriation $663,469 And that to meet said appropriation the sum of $363,469 be raised from the tax levy. COMMENT: In developing the budget for the fiscal year, the Town relies upon the state aid forecast in the Governor’s budget which is released in mid to late January; however, the final state budget is not typically approved until late June each year. In some years, the final state aid figures vary from the Governor’s original proposal. For Fiscal Year 2027, the final net state aid to Milton (after subtracting for state assessments) is projected to be $14,175,116, an increase of $363,469 (or 2.6%) from the Governor’s proposed budget. This article would amend the Fiscal Year 2027 Budget by appropriating this additional revenue to the Fiscal Year 2027 Reserve Fund, which is set aside for extraordinary or unanticipated expenses. Transfers from the Reserve Fund are subject to the approval of the Warrant Committee and may be transferred to any budget account. In Fiscal Year 2026, the Reserve Fund was used to help offset that year’s snow and ice removal deficit as well as two smaller unanticipated expenses. The final Fiscal Year 2027 net state aid amount of $14,175,116 is a $692,950, or a 5.1%, increase over Fiscal Year 2026. 10 ARTICLE 2 To see if the Town will vote to authorize the following transfers of surplus bond proceeds: (1) Transfer $350,001.35 of surplus proceeds from previously issued bonds which are no longer needed to complete the DPW Locker Room and Cemetery Garage project for which they were initially borrowed, to pay the costs of purchasing a replacement Fire Engine, as authorized by M.G.L. c. 44, §20; (2) Transfer $74,000.00 of surplus proceeds from previously issued bonds which are no longer needed to complete the Pine Tree Brook flood control dam rehabilitation project for which they were initially borrowed, to pay the costs of purchasing a replacement Fire Engine, as authorized by M.G.L. c. 44, §20; Submitted by the Select Board. RECOMMENDED that the Town vote to approve the article as printed in the Warrant. COMMENT: If the Town issues debt for projects, but does not fully use all of the borrowed funds for a project (referred to as “surplus bond proceeds”), there are several options by which the Town can apply those funds to expenses. For surplus bond proceeds less than $50,000, the Select Board may vote to apply them to debt service expenses. For surplus bond proceeds greater than $50,000, a Town Meeting vote is required to appropriate the surplus proceeds to another capital project. This article proposes to appropriate surplus proceeds from projects for which the funds are no longer needed to offset the cost of the acquisition of a replacement Fire Engine (to replace Engine 2 which operates out of the East Milton Station). An appropriation of $1.1 million for the replacement of Engine 2 was approved at the 2025 Annual Town Meeting with an expected delivery in Winter 2026. This article would result in the Town using $424,001.35 in surplus proceeds towards Engine 2’s replacement costs, reducing the maximum amount the Town would borrow from $1.1 million to $675,998.65. 11 ARTICLE 3 To see what sum of money the Town will vote to appropriate for the rehabilitation, replacement or enhancement of the Town's water system, and to authorize the Select Board, on behalf of the Town, to apply for and use federal, state, MWRA or other funds for this purpose, to determine how such appropriation shall be raised; whether by borrowing or otherwise; and to act on anything relating thereto. Submitted by the Select Board. RECOMMENDED that the sum of $2,280,000 be appropriated for the purpose of financing the rehabilitation, replacement or enhancement of the Town's water system, including costs incidental and related thereto; that to meet this appropriation, the Treasurer, with the approval of the Select Board, is authorized to borrow $2,280,000 under and pursuant to Chapter 44, Section 8 (5) of the General Laws, as amended, or any other enabling authority, and to issue bonds or notes of the Town therefor, and that the Select Board and hereby is authorized to accept and expend in addition to the foregoing appropriation one or more grants or gifts from the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority or any other public or private funding source. COMMENT: As a member of the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority ("MWRA"), the Town has access to water system improvement funding through ten-year, 0% interest loans. This provides the primary source of funding for capital investments into the Town's watermains and requires appropriation by Town Meeting. The Town has previously appropriated $1,790,100 for water main improvements by votes of the Town Meeting at the 2024, 2025, and 2026 Annual Town Meetings. The Department of Public Works is preparing a package of water main improvement projects and is seeking the opportunity to increase the total appropriation available to complete more work as part of a larger bid package. The additional appropriation in this article would support replacement of aging water mains on Governors Road, Franklin Street, and Bassett Street. The Governors Road mains, originally installed in 1915 and 1932, experienced a water main break in May 2026 and have reached the end of their useful service life. The Franklin Street water main, installed in 1929, has experienced several breaks in recent years, highlighting the need for replacement. Replacing the water mains on Franklin and Bassett Streets at this time would allow the Town to coordinate utility and roadway improvements with the ongoing Franklin/Bassett apartment development. Completing this work concurrently will help reduce construction costs, improve project efficiency, and minimize future disruptions to residents, businesses, and the traveling public. Construction is anticipated to occur during the 2027 and 2028 construction season. Additional funding will enable the Town to address critical infrastructure needs proactively, improve system reliability, and reduce the likelihood of future emergency repairs and service disruptions. 12 ARTICLE 4 To see if the Town will approve a project and grant funding, as recommended by the Community Preservation Committee for Fiscal Year 2027, for the rehabilitation, restoration, and/or improvements to the playground at the Tucker School, provided that the project must enter into a Grant Agreement with the Town and submit regular progress and budget reports; and to act on anything relating thereto. text: TOWN OF NORWELL WARRANT Transcript of Articles in the Warrant for the SPECIAL and ANNUAL TOWN MEETING MONDAY, MAY 4, 2026 7:00 P.M. Goldman Gymnasium 328 Main Street Intentionally left blank 2 TOWN OF NORWELL WARRANT Special Town Meeting and Annual Town Meeting Monday, May 4, 2026 At 7:00 o'clock in the evening at Norwell Middle School Plymouth, ss. To one of the Constables of the Town of Norwell, in said County of Plymouth, Commonwealth of Massachusetts. GREETINGS: In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are hereby directed to notify and warn the inhabitants of the Town of Norwell, who being qualified to vote in elections and Town affairs, to meet at the Norwell Middle School, 328 Main Street, in said Norwell, on Monday, the fourth day of May, 2026 at 7:00p.m.; then and there to act upon the enclosed Articles, to wit: In case all Articles of the foregoing Warrant shall not be acted upon at the Meeting called for on Monday, May 4, 2026, to meet in Adjourned Sessions at such time and place as the meeting shall determine. This building is accessible to the handicapped and designated parking is provided. If requested, at least one week before the meeting, Warrants with large print can be available. Anyone requiring a Sign Language Interpreter should call the Town Clerk's office at least two weeks before the Special Town Meeting and Annual Town Meeting at 781-659-8072. 3 Town of Norwell: Report of the Advisory Board 2026 Special and Annual Town Meeting To the Citizens of Norwell: On Monday, May 4, 2026, the Town of Norwell will hold a Special Town Meeting followed by its Annual Town Meeting. The Special Town Meeting will cover business matters that must be acted upon before the end of this fiscal year, which is June 30, 2026. During the annual Town Meeting, the citizens of Norwell will vote on a budget for Fiscal Year 2027, as well as many other matters of interest to the Town. We encourage Town residents to review the Warrant. Voters attending Town Meeting responsibly discuss, debate, and determine Norwell’s budget for the upcoming year. The Advisory Board’s role is to advise residents of its recommendations on each Article contained in this Warrant. These recommendations have been determined following several months of evaluation and careful consideration of all the materials provided by Town Departments, Boards, and Committees. Every proposed article was reviewed by the Advisory Board with a presentation from its proponents in a public meeting. The intent of the budget is to provide appropriate funds to support ongoing operations, address capital and infrastructure needs, and maintain the Town’s fiscal health. All departments, boards, and committees continue to work with a common purpose to identify efficiencies and methods to better address budgetary challenges while delivering services to the residents of the Town of Norwell. We would like to thank the residents, employees, and volunteers across all Departments, Boards, and Committees for their invaluable input. In particular, we extend our gratitude to Ellen McKenna for her exceptional support to the Advisory Board. We also wish to formally thank Christine McCarthy, Finance Director, for her professional guidance and dedicated support throughout this entire process. We extend special thanks to Darleen Sullivan, Town Administrator, who is retiring after many years of outstanding service to the Town of Norwell. Her leadership, expertise, and unwavering commitment have been instrumental in guiding the Town through countless challenges and successes, and we are deeply grateful for her many contributions. It is important that your voice is heard. We look forward to seeing you at Town Meeting on May 4, 2026. Sincerely, The Norwell Advisory Board John LaCara, Chair Bob Perniola, Vice Chair Stephen Bright Patricia Grueter Matthew Hanson Lucas Hamory Bob Howard Ann Mulligan Matthew Weinmann 4 TOWN BUDGET Glossary of Terms Appropriation: An authorization to make expenditures and to incur obligations for specific purposes. An appropriation is granted by Town Meeting and is usually limited in time and amount as to when it may be expended. Any part of the general appropriation not spent or encumbered by June 30 automatically reverts to surplus. A specific appropriation is carried forward from year to year until spent for the designated purpose or transferred by Town Meeting vote to another account. Assessed Valuation: A valuation set upon real or personal property by the Board of Assessors as a basis for levying taxes. Budget: A plan of financial operation consisting of an estimate of proposed expenditures for a given period and the means of financing them. The budget is voted in the spring at Town Meeting for the fiscal year that begins the following July 1st. Capital Budget: A plan of proposed capital outlays and the means of financing them for the current year. Cherry Sheet: An annual statement received from the Massachusetts Department of Revenue detailing estimated receipts for the next fiscal year and the estimated state and county government charges payable. These amounts are used by the assessors in setting the tax rate. The actual receipts and charges may vary from the estimates. Community Preservation Act (CPA): The Town adopted the Community Preservation Act (CPA) in 2002. This Act allows the town to collect a 3% surcharge on property tax bills (the funds can be matched up to 100% by the state when funds are available), which creates the Community Preservation Fund, to use for Community Preservation purposes. Each year, the town must appropriate, or reserve (but not necessarily spend), 10% of the funds for each of the three Community Preservation purposes: Open Space, Historic Resources, and Community Housing. The remaining 70% of the funds can be appropriated, reserved or used for any of the three purposes and for Recreation and administration. Debt Service: Payment of interest and repayment of principal to holders of the Town’s debt instruments. Fiscal Year: A 12-month period, commencing July 1 and ending June 30, to which the annual budget applies. Fiscal years are often denoted FYXX with the last two numbers representing the calendar year in which it ends, for example FY25 is the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025. Free Cash: Free cash is the portion of unreserved fund balance available for appropriation. 5 It is not cash but rather is approximately the total of cash and receivables, less current liabilities and earmarked reserves, reduced also by reserves for uncollected taxes. This is also referred to as “available cash”. The amount is certified annually by the Massachusetts Department of Revenue. General Fund: The major town owned fund which is created with town receipts and which is charged with expenditures payable from revenues. Grant: A contribution of assets by one governmental unit or other organization to another. Typically, these contributions are made to local governments from the state and federal governments. Grants are usually made for specific purposes. Line-Item Budget: A format of budgeting that organizes costs by type of expenditure such as expenses, equipment, and salaries. Overlay: The amount set aside to allow for uncollected property taxes. An amount for overlay is added to the appropriations and other charges. The “Overlay Surplus” is the portion of each year’s overlay account no longer required to cover property tax abatements. Overlay Surplus: The unused amount of the overlay for prior years, which may be transferred, by vote of the Town, to the reserve account or used for any lawful purpose. Property Tax Levy: The amount produced by multiplying the assessed valuation of property by the tax rate. The tax rate is expressed “per thousand dollars” of assessed valuation. Reserve Fund: Money set aside by Town Meeting to be allocated by the Advisory Board for extraordinary or unforeseen expenditures. Stabilization Fund: A special reserve funded by Town Meeting for future expenditures. The Town has also established Athletic Fields Stabilization, Capital Stabilization and Special Education Stabilization funds. Terms associated with Proposition 2½: Debt or Capital Exclusion: The Town can assess taxes in excess of the levy limit by voting a debt exclusion or capital outlay exclusion. This amount does not become a permanent part of the levy limit base, but allows the Town to assess taxes for a specific period of time in excess of the limit for payment of debt service costs or for payment of capital expenditures. Excess Levy Capacity: The difference between the Town's tax levy limit and its actual tax levy for the current year. It is the additional tax levy that could be raised without asking for an override. New Growth: The amount of property tax revenue that the Town can add to its allowable tax levy as a result of new construction, alterations, subdivisions or change of use, which 6 increases the value of a parcel of land by more than certain amounts. Override: An amount voted by the Town, which is permanently added to the levy limit. A majority vote of the Selectmen allows an override question to be put on the ballot. Override questions must be presented in dollar terms and must specify the purpose of the override. Overrides require a majority vote of approval by the Town Meeting and by ballot question. Tax Levy Limit: The maximum amount of the tax levy for a period under the restrictions of Proposition 2½. It is calculated as the prior year limit plus new growth plus 2.5% of the prior year levy limit. 7 Index of Articles for the 2026 Special Town Meeting Article Purpose Submitted By Page 1 Unpaid Bills from Prior Fiscal Years Finance Director 9 2 Rescind Remaining Balance of Authorized But Unused Debt Finance Director 10 3 Article Language: Use of PFAS Settlement Funds for Water Treatment Plant Study Finance Director 10 4 Use of Overlay Surplus to Fund Senior Work Finance Director Program Employer PR Tax Expenses 10 5 Snow and Ice Deficit Highway Surveyor 11 6 Maintenance of Artificial Turf Fields Highway Surveyor 11 7 Affordable Housing Acquisition, Creation, Preservation (AH) Community Preservation Committee 11 8 Electric Rehab of Town Common Community Preservation Committee 12 9 East Boardwalk Modification, Phase III Community Preservation Committee 12 8 TOWN OF NORWELL Commonwealth of Massachusetts WARRANT FOR SPECIAL TOWN MEETING Monday, May 4, 2026 At 7:00 O’clock in the Evening Norwell Middle School, 328 Main Street Henry E. text: Norfolk, ss. COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS SPECIAL TOWN MEETING WARRANT TOWN OF NORWOOD To either of the constables in the Town of Norwood in said County, Greetings: In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are hereby required to notify and warn the inhabitants of the Town of Norwood, qualified as the law requires to vote in Town affairs, to meet in the Auditorium of the Norwood High School at 245 Nichols Street in said town on Monday, November 13, 2023, at six-thirty o’clock in the evening. In the event that all business is not completed on November 13, said Meeting may be adjourned until a following Monday or Thursday, as determined by Town Meeting; and at such time act on the following articles, namely: ARTICLE 1. To see if the Town will vote to amend Article XXXIV (Rules of Procedure for Norwood Representative Town Meeting) of the By-Laws of the Town of Norwood as follows; a. Amend Section 4 (Physical Conditions), by deleting the second sentence in the fourth paragraph, “The badge will contain the member’s picture, name, and district number.” b. Amend Section 9 (Method of Taking Votes), by adding use of electronic voting devices and show of hands as methods of taking votes in the first sentence in the first paragraph, so that said first sentence shall read: Unless otherwise voted by the membership prior to the taking of a vote, all votes requiring a majority will be by voice, i.e.: “Aye” or “No;” by use of electronic voting devices; by show of hands; or by a non-counted standing vote as decided by the Moderator. Or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 2. To see if the Town will vote to receive and accept the Report of the Town Meeting Size Committee; and further, to see if the Town will vote to amend Article I, Section 2 (Act to Establish Representative Town Meeting) of the By-Laws of the Town of Norwood, by deleting the present text and replacing it with the following text: 1 % per cent of the total registered voters of the town and rounding up to the nearest number divisible by nine in addition to the members at large shall constitute a representative town meeting in the Town of Norwood. The amendment shall take effect on April 7, 2025. Or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 3. To see if the Town will vote to amend the General By-Laws by deleting Article XVII (Permanent Building Construction Committee) of the By-Laws in its entirety, and replacing it with a new proposed By-Law, which reads: ARTICLE XVII PERMANENT BUILDING PROJECTS Section 1: Definitions "Project" means the design and construction, reconstruction, installation, or demolition of any municipal building or structure as described in M.G.L. c.7C, sec. 44-58; c. 30, sec.39M; c.149 sect. 44A through 44H; and c. 149A, except for those buildings and structures of the Norwood Municipal Light Department or the Norwood Housing Authority. "Client" means the town department, board or committee having day to day control of the facility in which a project will take place. "Design" is the schematic design, the design development, and the preparation of construction documents developed from the goals established by the proposed client. "Construction" includes all steps necessary to implement or complete a project from design through completion and acceptance of the Project. Section 2: Project Requirements and Notifications: Any client that intends to propose a project for Town Meeting approval shall provide information regarding the project goals and financial requirements of the project to the Director of the Facilities Department (Director of Facilities) at least one hundred eighty (180) days in advance of the Town Meeting at which funding for the project will be requested, unless the project is emergency in nature, in which case said notification shall be as soon as practical. The Director of Facilities shall forthwith notify the General Manager, Selectmen, Finance Commission, and Capital Outlay Committee of the proposed project. The Director of Facilities or his/her designee shall estimate an initial design and project cost and whether an Owner’s Project Manager shall be required in accordance with Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 149 section 44A1/2 and Chapter 149A Section.3. Section 3: Supervision of Project Construction The Director of Facilities or his/her designee shall administer all Phases of Projects as defined herein with a cost estimated to be less than that requiring an Owner's Project Manager. All project feasibility studies shall be undertaken by the Director of Facilities. The Director of Facilities shall work closely at all times with the Client to ensure that the design and construction meets the needs of the Client. For Projects requiring the hiring of an Owner's Project Manager a Project Specific Committee (the Project Committee) at the discretion of the Representative Town Meeting may be appointed consisting of the Director of Facilities, a representative of the Client, and three residents appointed by the Selectmen. In making appointments to the Project Committee the Selectmen shall make every effort to ensure that at a minimum at least one (1) of the three (3) individuals appointed has relevant and significant experience as an architect, an engineer, a construction supervisor, or is someone who has been primarily engaged in the construction industry. The general duties of the Project Committee shall be to assist the Director of Facilities in selecting an Owner's Project Manager and in selecting a Designer in accordance with appropriate law. The Project Committee shall review and approve construction drawings and documents to ensure that they meet the Client’s intended needs. The Project Committee shall review Change Orders in a timely fashion and make a recommendation to the General Manager, who shall have final approval of any Change Orders. Construction Contract Awards shall be made by the General Manager. Section 4: Appropriations All funds appropriated for a Project as defined by this By-Law shall be overseen by the General Manager. No payments for any requisition for payment related to the Project shall be made without the General Manager’s approval. Section 5: Records All drawings, documents, and specifications shall be retained in accordance with Massachusetts General Laws and turned over to the Facilities Department. Or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 4. To see if the Town will vote to amend the By-Laws by adding a new Article, the number of which shall be assigned by the Town Clerk, which reads: Interest on Overdue Bills For Police Details and Fire Detail: Pursuant to MGL Chapter 40, Section 21E, payment of bills issued by the Town of Norwood for police details and fire details shall be due on the thirtieth day following the date of issuance. The rate on which interest shall accrue if such bills remain unpaid after such due date shall be fixed at the same rate at which interest accrues on unpaid real estate tax bills issued by the Town of Norwood. Or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 5. To see if the Town will vote, pursuant to Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40, Section 59, and Chapter 23A, Sections 3A through 3F, and the applicable regulations thereunder, to: (a) approve a Tax Increment Financing Agreement (“TIF Agreement”) between the Town, FM Global, and Neponset River, LLC for property shown on Assessors Map 15, Sheet 15, Lot 7, which TIF Agreement provides for real estate tax exemptions over a twenty (20)-year period at the exemption rate schedule set forth therein; and (b) authorize the Board of Selectmen to execute a TIF Agreement, and any documents related thereto, and to approve submission to the Massachusetts Economic Assistance Coordinating Council (EACC) of the TIF Agreement, and any documents related thereto, all relating to the project as described in the TIF Agreement, and any necessary documents relating thereto, and related submissions, and to take such other actions as necessary or appropriate to implement those documents, and carry out the purposes of this article; (c) Or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 6. To see if the Town will vote, pursuant to Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40, Section 59, and Chapter 23A, Sections 3A through 3F, and the applicable regulations thereunder, to: (a) amend a Tax Increment Financing Agreement (“TIF Agreement”) between the Town, FM Global, and Neponset River, LLC approved by Norwood Town Meeting on May 9, 2011, and executed by the Town and FM Global and Neponset River, LLC on May 9, 2011 for property shown on Assessors Map 15, Sheet 13, Lot 1B, which TIF Agreement provides for real estate tax exemptions over a twenty (20)-year period at the exemption rate schedule set forth therein; and (b) authorize the Board of Selectmen to execute an Amended TIF Agreement, and any documents related thereto, and to approve submission to the Massachusetts Economic Assistance Coordinating Council (EACC) of the TIF Agreement, and any documents related thereto, all relating to the project as described in the TIF Agreement, and any necessary documents relating thereto, and related submissions, and to take such other actions as necessary or appropriate to 4 implement those documents, and carry out the purposes of this article; (c) Or take any other action in the matter. ARTICLE 7. To see if the Town will vote to update the current Stretch Energy Code, Article XLVIII of the General By-Laws, to include the Municipal Opt-in Specialized Stretch Energy Code (the “Specialized Energy Code”) for the purpose of regulating the design and construction of buildings for the effective use of energy and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, pursuant to the entirety of 225 CMR 22 and 23 including Appendices RC and CC, including future editions, amendments or modifications thereto, provided that said adoption of the Specialized Energy Code and this amendment of the By-Laws shall be effective as of July 1, 2024. As amended, Article XLVIII shall read: Article XLVI STRETCH ENERGY CODE WITH OPT-IN SPECIALIZED ENERGY CODE 2023 Section 1. Definitions International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) — The International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) is a building energy code created by the International Code Council. It is a model code adopted by many state and municipal governments in the United States for the establishment of minimum design and construction requirements for energy efficiency, and is updated on a three-year cycle. The baseline energy conservation requirements of the Massachusetts State Building Code are the IECC 2021 with Massachusetts amendments, as approved by the Massachusetts Board of Building Regulations and Standards and published in state regulations as part of 730 CMR. Stretch Energy Code - Codified by the combination of 225 CMR 22 and 23, not including Appendices RC and CC, the Stretch Energy Code is a comprehensive set of amendments to the International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) seeking to achieve all lifecycle cost-effective energy efficiency in accordance with the Green Communities Act of 2008, as well as to reduce the climate impacts of buildings built to this code. Specialized Energy Code — Codified by the entirety of 225 CMR 22 and 23 including Appendices RC and CC, the Specialized Energy Code adds residential and commercial appendices to the Massachusetts Stretch Energy Code, based on amendments to the respective net-zero appendices of the International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) to incorporate the energy efficiency of the Stretch Energy Code and further reduce the climate impacts of buildings built to this code, with the goal of achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from the buildings sector no later than 2050. Section 2. Purpose The purpose of 225 CMR 22.00 and 23.00 including Appendices RC and CC, also referred to as the Specialized Energy Code, is to provide a more energy efficient and low greenhouse gas emissions alternative to the Stretch Energy Code or the baseline Massachusetts Energy Code, applicable to the relevant sections of the Massachusetts State Building Code for both new construction and existing buildings. Section 3. Applicability The Specialized Energy Code shall apply to residential and commercial buildings. Buildings not included in this scope shall comply with the Stretch Energy Code, as applicable. Section 4. Adoption The Specialized Energy Code is herein incorporated by reference into the By-Laws. Section 5. Enforcement The Specialized Energy Code shall be enforceable by the Building Inspector. Section 6. Effective Date This By-Law shall take effect on July 1, 2024. text: TOWN OF PLAINVILLE Transcript of Articles in the Warrant for the ANNUAL TOWN MEETING Report of the Finance Committee Monday, May 18, 2026 At 7:00 p.m. Please bring this report to the meeting for use in the proceedings at the BEATRICE H. WOOD ELEMENTARY SCHOOL 72 Messenger Street TABLE OF CONTENTS A Letter from the Select Board 2 Call to the Annual Town Meeting 3 Finance Committee Report 4 FY2027 Revenue & Expenditure Budget Estimate 5 Glossary of Terms 6 Index of Annual Town Meeting Articles 9 Annual Town Meeting Articles 11 Appendix 1 – Parliamentary Procedures 39 Appendix 2 – Report of the Planning Board 41 Appendix 3 – Finance Committee Recommended Sources of Funds 44 Appendix 4 – Consent Agenda 46 - IMPORTANT This Warrant contains Articles, explanations, recommendations, and appendices. Only the Articles are part of the “official” call to Town Meeting. The explanations and appendices are editorial, and the recommendations expressed are those of the Finance Committee. Only the Articles are part of the official Town Meeting warrant. 1|Page The Select Board To the Townspeople of Plainville, We are pleased to present the Warrant for the Annual Town Meeting to be held on Monday, May 18, 2026 at 7 p.m. at the Wood School. Town Meeting remains the cornerstone of our local democracy, providing residents with the opportunity to directly participate in the decisions that shape our community. We encourage all eligible voters to attend, ask questions, and take part in the important work before us. This year’s Warrant reflects a careful balance between maintaining essential services, investing in critical infrastructure, and exercising fiscal discipline. The Town continues to face significant financial pressures, including rising costs associated with health insurance, special education, and other fixed obligations. As a result, difficult decisions were required to prioritize needs over wants, defer certain initiatives, and focus on the long-term financial stability of the Town. Among the articles presented are several important capital and infrastructure investments, including applying for and accepting state roadway funds and grants for improvements, water system upgrades, and public safety equipment, many of which leverage state or federal funding opportunities. The Warrant also includes zoning updates, policy refinements, and other measures intended to support thoughtful growth and enhance the quality of life in Plainville. We thank the Finance Committee, Town staff, and our boards and committees for their hard work in developing the articles and recommendations contained in this Warrant. We look forward to a productive and respectful Town Meeting and appreciate your continued engagement and commitment to the Town of Plainville. THE SELECT BOARD Jeffrey Johnson, Chair Brian Kelly, Vice-Chair Steven Albert, Clerk 2|Page TOWN OF PLAINVILLE Commonwealth of Massachusetts WARRANT FOR THE ANNUAL TOWN MEETING Monday, May 18, 2026 At 7:00 o’clock in the Evening at the Beatrice H. Wood Elementary School, 72 Messenger Street Norfolk, ss To any of the Constables of the Town of Plainville, in said County of Norfolk, Commonwealth of Massachusetts. GREETINGS: In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are hereby directed to notify and warn the inhabitants of the Town of Plainville, who are qualified to vote in elections and Town affairs, to meet at the Beatrice H. Wood Elementary School, 72 Messenger Street, in said Plainville, on Monday, the 18th day of May, 2026 at 7:00 p.m.; then and there to act upon the enclosed articles, to wit: In case all articles in the foregoing Warrant shall not be acted upon at the Meeting called for on Monday, May 18, 2026, to meet in Adjourned Sessions at such time and place as the meeting shall determine. This building is accessible to the handicapped, and designated parking is provided. If requested, at least one week before the meeting, large-print warrants can be available. Please call the Town Clerk’s office at least one week before the Town Meeting at 508-576-8451. 3|Page Town of Plainville Report of the Finance Committee Dear Plainville Taxpayers, The Finance Committee is pleased to present the Fiscal Year 2027 budget for your consideration at this year’s Annual Town Meeting. This has been a particularly challenging budget cycle. The Town continues to experience significant cost increases in areas largely outside of local control, including health insurance, special education, retirement obligations, and contractual commitments. At the same time, revenue growth remains constrained under Proposition 2½, slow new growth and diminishing state aid, requiring the Committee to make difficult decisions to ensure that the budget remains balanced. In response to these pressures, the Committee worked closely with Town staff and departments to prioritize essential services and core municipal functions. This process required a disciplined approach, including the deferral of certain capital requests, reductions in discretionary spending, and a general pullback from initiatives that, while valuable, are not feasible within the Town’s current fiscal capacity. The result is a budget that maintains the Town’s fundamental services while positioning Plainville to remain financially stable in the year ahead. The Committee recognizes that some needs remain unmet and will continue to monitor conditions throughout the year, with the potential to revisit certain items at a future Town Meeting should additional resources become available. We appreciate the cooperation and professionalism of Town departments, boards, and staff throughout this process, and we thank the residents of Plainville for their continued support and engagement. With warm regards and anticipation, The Plainville Finance Committee, Mark Johnson, Chairman Nicholas Sammarco, Vice-Chairman David Rabinovitz, Clerk Richard Comeau Chris Brenneis Carol Lerch 4|Page Town of Plainville FY27 Revenue & Expenditure Budget Estimate Includes Other Sources of Funds Revenue & Expenditures FY2027 X REVENUE: Property Taxes Prior Year Levy Limit Proposition 2.5 New Growth Override Tax Levy limit Debt Exclusion (Town) Debt Exclusion (Sewer) Allowance for Abatements/Exemptions Maximum Allowable Tax Levy State Aid: Cherry Sheet Receipts Cherry Sheet Assessments Local Receipts: Local Receipts Other Available Funds: Gaming Stabilization Fund Bridge Stabilization Fund Transfers from Enterprise Funds Transfers from State Revolving Fund $ 32,667,461 816,687 350,000 - 33,834,148 237,586 (100,000) X X X $ 33,971,734 4,403,371 (1,013,640) $ 3,389,731 $ 4,511,189 2,148,538 839,264 774,235 125,000 $ 3,887,037 Total Operational Revenue $ 45,759,691 Free Cash $ TOTAL REVENUE $ 47,693,364 EXPENDITURES Total Appropriations (Budgets) Transfer to Enterprise Tax Title Reserve for Articles Transfer to General Stabilization Transfer to Capital Stabilization X TOTAL EXPENDITURES 5|Page X X 1,933,673 45,647,495 112,196 $ 45,759,691 1,933,673 $ 1,933,673 $ 47,693,364 GLOSSARY OF TERMS Appropriation: An authorization to make expenditures and to incur obligations for specific purposes. An appropriation is granted by Town Meeting and is usually limited in time and amount as to when it may be expended. Any part of the general appropriation not spent or encumbered by June 30th automatically reverts to surplus, which may become Free Cash. A specific appropriation is carried forward from year to year until spent for the designated purpose or transferred by Town Meeting vote to another account. Assessed Valuation: A valuation set upon real or personal property by the Board of Assessors as a basis for levying taxes. Budget: A plan of financial operation consisting of an estimate of proposed expenditures for a given period and the means of financing them. The budget is voted at the Annual Town Meeting for the fiscal year that begins the following July 1st. Capital Budget: A plan of proposed capital outlays and the means of financing them for the current year. Cherry Sheet: An annual statement received from the Massachusetts Department of Revenue detailing estimated payments to the Town for the next fiscal year and the estimated state and county government charges payable by the Town. The Assessors in setting the tax rate use these amounts. The actual receipts and charges may vary from the estimates. Community Preservation Act (CPA): The Town adopted the Community Preservation Act (CPA) in 2019. This Act allows the Town to collect up to a 3% surcharge (Plainville has voted 1%) on property tax bills (the funds can be matched up to 100% by the state when funds are available), which creates the Community Preservation Fund, to use for Community Preservation purposes. Each year, the town must appropriate, or reserve (but not necessarily spend), 10% of the funds for each of the three Community Preservation purposes: Open Space, Historic Resources, and Community Housing. The remaining 70% of the funds can be appropriated or reserved for any of the three purposes and for Recreation and/or for administration. Consent Agenda: A consent agenda’s purpose is to act expeditiously upon certain types of articles that historically have generated no controversy and can reasonably be voted upon without debate. With a consent agenda, several articles can be addressed with a single vote, thereby ensuring that a greater proportion of the town meeting's time is dedicated to articles that are the subject of genuine debate. See the Appendix in the back of this Town Meeting Warrant. Debt or Capital Exclusion: The Town can assess taxes in excess of the levy limit by voting a debt exclusion or capital outlay exclusion. This amount does not become a permanent part of the levy limit base but does allow the Town to assess taxes for a specific period in excess of the limit for payment of debt service costs or payment of capital expenditures. Debt Service: Payment of interest and repayment of principal to holders of the Town’s debt. Enterprise Fund: An Enterprise Fund is a type of municipal accounting mechanism used to manage the finances of a specific service or utility—such as water, sewer, or solid waste (trash and recycling) —in a manner similar to a private business. Under an enterprise fund, all revenues and expenses associated with providing the service are tracked separately from the general fund. The service is intended to be self-supporting, meaning that user fees and charges (rather than taxes) are the primary funding source. 6|Page This approach promotes transparency and ensures that the true cost of providing the service is visible to both administrators and ratepayers. It allows for better long-term financial planning, including capital investment, maintenance, and debt service for the utility. Enterprise funds are authorized under MGL Chapter 44, Section 53F½ and must be formally adopted by Town Meeting. Once established, the fund operates with its own budget, and any surplus (retained earnings) may be used for future utility-related needs, subject to appropriation. Excess Levy Capacity: The difference between the Town’s tax levy limit and its actual tax levy for the current year. It is the additional tax levy that could be raised without asking for an override. Fiscal Year: A 12-month period, commencing July 1 and ending June 30th, to which the annual budget applies. Fiscal years are often denoted FYXX with the last two numbers representing the calendar year in which it ends, for example, FY27 is the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. Free Cash: Free cash is the portion of the unreserved fund balance available for appropriation. It is not cash but rather is approximately the total of cash and receivables less current liabilities and earmarked reserves also reduced by reserves for uncollected taxes. This is also referred to as “available cash”. The amount is certified annually by the Massachusetts Department of Revenue. General Fund: The major town-owned fund is created with town receipts and is charged with expenditures payable from revenues. Grant: A contribution of assets by one governmental unit or other organization to another. Typically, these contributions are made to local governments from the state and federal governments. Grants are usually made for specific purposes. Line-Item Budget: A format of budgeting that organizes costs by type of expenditure such as expenses, equipment, and salaries. New Growth: The amount of property tax revenue that the Town can add to its allowable tax levy as a result of new construction, alterations, subdivisions or change of use which increases the value of a parcel of land by more than certain amounts. OPEB: Other Post-Employment Benefits. Benefits that an employee of the Town will receive in retirement. OPEB does not include pension benefits paid to the retired employee. Other benefits include insurance premiums, healthcare premiums, and deferred-compensation contractual arrangements. Overlay: The amount set aside to allow for uncollected property taxes. An amount for the overlay is added to the appropriations and other charges. Overlay Surplus – see below. Overlay Surplus: The unused amount of the overlay from prior years, which may be transferred, by a vote of the Town, to the reserve account or used for extraordinary items. Override: An amount, voted by the Town, which is permanently added to the levy limit. A majority vote of the Select Board allows an override question to be put on the ballot. Override questions must be presented in dollar terms and must specify the purpose of the override. Overrides require a majority vote of approval by the Town. Property Tax Levy: The amount produced by multiplying the assessed valuation of property by the tax rate. The tax rate is expressed “per thousand dollars” of assessed valuation. 7|Page Reserve Fund: Money set aside by Town Meeting to be allocated by the Finance Committee for extraordinary or unforeseen expenditures. Stabilization Fund: A special reserve funded by Town Meeting for future expenditures. Tax Classification Tax Allocation: Before setting the tax rate each year, a classification hearing is held by the Select Board to determine the shares of the tax levy to be paid by each class of property in the community, and whether to allow an open space discount, residential exemption, or small commercial exemption. The Assessors provide information about the impact of these options at the hearing. The decisions of the Select Board are reported to the Bureau of Accounts and are referred to as the “Classification Tax Allocation.” Tax Levy Limit: The maximum amount of the tax levy for a period under the restrictions of Proposition 2½. text: TOWN OF PLYMOUTH FALL ANNUAL TOWN MEETING WARRANT Saturday, October 17, 2026 To the Town Clerk of the Town of Plymouth, Commonwealth of Massachusetts: GREETINGS: In the name of the Commonwealth, you are directed to notify and warn the Inhabitants of Plymouth, qualified to consider and vote on articles at the Fall Annual Town Meeting of the Town of Plymouth, to meet in a hybrid format, on Saturday, the Seventeenth day of October, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., with information necessary for the Moderator, Town Meeting members, Town officials and interested members of the public to access and witness the deliberations and actions taken at the Town Meeting as follows: Town Meeting members will have the option to be in person at Plymouth North High School at 41 Obery Street in Plymouth, MA using an electronic voting clicker to take actions or remotely using telecast through Zoom Webinar videoconferencing platform for their deliberations and the use of V-Voter to take actions remotely. Town Officials will provide information through the Zoom Webinar videoconferencing platform. Interested members of the public will be able to view the meeting through the Plymouth local government channel (The Local Seen) available on Comcast and Verizon, or thelocalseen.media/live. Individuals not otherwise lawfully entitled to speak will have the opportunity to speak through the Zoom Webinar videoconferencing platform with forty-eight (48) hours advanced notice given to and permission granted by the Town Moderator. Registered Town of Plymouth voters wishing to participate in the hybrid Fall Annual Town Meeting shall submit a request to participate in the Meeting to the Town Clerk not less than fortyeight (48) hours in advance of the Town Meeting scheduled for Saturday, October 17, 2026, commencing at 8:00 a.m. Upon receipt of the request and verification of the requester’s voter registration status, the Town Clerk shall provide to the requester instructions for participating in the remote Town Meeting. To act on the following articles to wit: ARTICLE 1: Budget Amendment – Visitor’s Center Capital Funds To see if the Town will vote to amend the vote taken under Article 4 Item A9 of the 2025 Fall Annual Town Meeting warrant to reduce the Capital appropriations for the Visitor’s Center Addition by a sum of money, or take any other action relative thereto. TOWN MANAGER ARTICLE 2: Budget Amendment – Solid Waste Enterprise To see if the Town will vote to amend the votes taken under Article 10 of the 2026 Spring Annual Town Meeting warrant, and, as necessary, to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds, or borrow funds for the purpose of supplementing enterprise departmental expenses, and/or to reduce certain departmental expenses or otherwise amend said vote, or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 3: Borrowing Authority Rescission Request To see if the Town will vote to rescind the remaining borrowing authority on Article 4B1 of the 2022 Spring Special Town Meeting, further amended by Article 10 of the 2023 Spring Special Town Meeting, for the Municipal Airport Sewerage Treatment Plant Upgrade, or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 4: FY26 Snow and Ice Deficit Funding Recommendation To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds a sum of money to fund the Fiscal Year 2026 Snow & Ice deficit that remains from the June 30, 2026, balance sheet, or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 5: Capital Recommendations To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds or borrow a sum of money for the construction and/or repair and/or purchase and/or lease and/or replacement of departmental buildings and/or equipment and/or capital facilities for various departments of the Town and/or for feasibility and other types of studies, including the payment of costs incidental or related thereto, and to authorize contracts or lease/purchase agreements for such purposes for terms of three or more years, as follows, ITEM A1 DEPARTMENT Finance PROJECT DESCRIPTION Communication Towers & Compound Maintenance Work A2 Purchase of a Motor Grader A6 Public Works – Highway Division Public Works – Maintenance Division Public Works – Maintenance Division Public Works – Maintenance Division Energy & Environment A7 Energy & Environment 0 Spooner Street Phase II Assessment A8 Energy & Environment Engineering & Permitting for Restoration of Gilmore Bogs A3 A4 A5 Parking Garage Repairs Town Hall Lighting Upgrade Main Library Transformer Replacement Downtown Resiliency Project A9 Public Works – Water Planning, Design and Permitting New Source Division or take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 6: Environmental Affairs Funding – Cyanobacteria Monitoring and Sampling To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds a sum of money to be used for ongoing monitoring and sampling of cyanobacteria blooms in local lakes and ponds, or take any other action relative thereto. DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT ARTICLE 7: Environmental Affairs Funding – Town Forest Fire Department Overtime To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds a sum of money to be used for staffing two Fire Department brush breakers during the prescribed burn at Town Forest, or take any other action relative thereto. DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT ARTICLE 8: Title Research Funding for Roads of Shallow Pond Estates To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds or borrow a sum of money for the purposes of title research, appraisals, legal fees, land surveying, drafting costs, and/or any other action required to prepare the roadways of Andrew’s Way, Barbara’s Way, Donna Drive, Kathleen Drive, Penny Lane, and Shallow Pond Way, for future acceptance as Public Ways, or take any other action relative thereto. DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS ARTICLE 9: Change 2027 Spring Town Meeting Date To see if the Town will vote to reschedule the 2027 Spring Annual Town Meeting from April 3, 2027, to April 24, 2027, as required by General Bylaws, Ch. 50, §3, or to take any other action relative thereto. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 10: Adoption of G.L. Ch. 39, §23D, Mullin Rule To see if the Town will vote to accept the provisions of G.L. Ch. 39, §23D, which provides that a member of a board, committee, or commission holding an adjudicatory hearing shall not be disqualified from voting in the matter solely due to the member's absence from one session of such hearing, provided that certain conditions are met; and provided further that such acceptance shall be applicable to all adjudicatory hearings opened on or after the effective date of the vote taken hereunder, or to take any other action relative thereto. TOWN MANAGER ARTICLE 11: Charter Amendment – Addition of Two Alternate Members to the Conservation Commission To see if the Town will vote to authorize the Select Board to petition the General Court to amend Section 3-10-1 of the current Charter in order to add two alternate members to the composition of the Conservation Commission by inserting the underlined as written below, provided, however, that the General Court may make clerical or editorial changes of form only to the bill, unless the Select Board approves amendments to the bill before enactment by the General Court, provided further that the Select Board is hereby authorized to approve amendments which shall be within the scope of the general public objectives, or, take any other action relative thereto. CHAPTER 3: THE EXECUTIVE BRANCH: THE SELECT BOARD, THE TOWN MANAGER AND PLANNING BOARD: Section 10: Conservation Commission 3-10-1: The Select Board shall appoint a Conservation Commission of seven (7) members and two (2) alternate members for three-year (3) overlapping terms. SELECT BOARD ARTICLE 12: General Bylaws Amendment – Discontinuation of Plymouth County Outreach (PCO) Revolving Fund To see if the Town will vote to amend the General Bylaws, Ch. 24, §13, Authorized Revolving Funds, to rescind the revolving fund known as Plymouth County Outreach (PCO), by deleting the strikethrough as written below, or take any other action relative thereto. A B Revolving Fund Plymouth County Outreach (PCO) C D E Department, Board, Committee, Agency or Program or Activity Officer Authorized to Fees, Charges or Other Expenses Payable from Spend from Fund Receipts Credited to Fund Fund Fiscal Years Chief of Police POLICE DEPARTMENT Annual dues collected from PCO member departments PCO Initiative to assist Fiscal year 2020 those struggling with subsequent years substance abuse disorders, mental health disorders, and/or behavioral health disorders and ARTICLE 13: General Bylaws Amendment – Demolition Delay To see if the Town will vote to amend the General Bylaws, Ch. 180, Historic District and Historic Preservation, §5, Intent and Purpose, and §6, Definitions, by inserting the underlined and deleting the strikethrough as written below, or take any other action relative thereto. § 180-5. Intent and purpose. The Demolition Delay Bylaw is enacted for the purpose of preserving and protecting significant buildings and other structures (barns or out-buildings which are generally associated with the significantly historic building) within the Town of Plymouth which constitute or reflect distinctive features of the architectural, cultural, economic, political or social history of the Town and to limit the detrimental effect of demolition on the character of the Town. Through this bylaw, owners of preferably preserved buildings are encouraged to seek out alternative options that will preserve, rehabilitate or restore such buildings and residents of the Town are alerted to impending demolitions of significant buildings. By preserving and protecting significant buildings, streetscapes and neighborhoods, this bylaw promotes the public welfare by making the Town a more attractive and desirable place in which to live and work. To achieve these purposes, the Plymouth Historic District Commission Historical Commission is authorized to advise the Building Commissioner with respect to demolition permit applications. The issuance of demolition permits is regulated as provided by this bylaw. § 180-6. Definitions. As used in this article, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated: COMMISSION — The Plymouth Historic District Commission Historical Commission. TOWN MANAGER ARTICLE 14: Zoning Bylaw Amendment – Senior Housing To see if the Town will vote to amend the Zoning Bylaw by replacing the word “Elderly” with “Senior”, modifying the definition of “Elderly Household” in §201-3, modifying the parking table in §203-7 related to certain senior housing uses, and prohibiting the existing Elderly Housing use in the General Commercial, Arterial Commercial, and Mixed Commerce Zoning Districts as listed in the Use Table, all by inserting the underlined and deleting the strikethrough as documented on file with the Town Clerk, “Zoning Bylaw Amendment – Senior Housing”, or take any other action relative thereto. PLANNING BOARD ARTICLE 15: Zoning Bylaw Amendment – Industrial Zoning Update To see if the Town will vote to amend the Zoning Bylaw by reducing setback and Special Permit requirements in the Light Industrial Building Height Overlay District (LIBHOD), exempting mechanical equipment from the height measurement calculation in the Light Industrial District within the Dimensional Table, and eliminating the 0.25 maximum Floor Area Ratio requirement for Light Industry and Renewable/Alternate Energy Manufacturing uses in the Use Table, all by inserting the underlined and deleting the strikethrough as documented on file with the Town Clerk, “Zoning Bylaw Amendment – Industrial Zoning Update”, or take any other action relative thereto. PLANNING BOARD ARTICLE 16: Zoning Bylaw Amendment – Data Centers Zoning To see if the Town will vote to amend the Zoning Bylaw, §201-3, Definitions, by adding a definition for “Data Center”, and by creating a new section, §207-12, Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers, which would enact a one-year temporary moratorium from October 17, 2026, until October 16, 2027 on the application, permitting, construction, expansion, or conversion of any Data Center to provide the Plymouth Planning Board with sufficient time to research and understand this complex use so that reasonable regulations may be developed for consideration at the Fall 2027 Special Town Meeting, all by inserting the underlined as documented on file with the Town Clerk, “Zoning Bylaw Amendment – Data Centers Zoning”, or take any other action relative thereto. PLANNING BOARD ARTICLE 17: Title V Repair Fund To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, transfer from available funds, or borrow a sum of money, for the purposes of financing the following water pollution abatement facility projects: sewer tie-ins or the repair, replacement and/or upgrade of septic systems, pursuant to agreements between the Board of Health and residential property owners; including without limitation, the payment of all costs thereof as defined in G.L. Ch. 29C §1; and to meet this appropriation the Treasurer with approval of the Select Board is authorized to borrow under G.L. Ch. 44 and/or G.L. Ch. 29C, or any other enabling authority, which amount may be borrowed through the Massachusetts Clean Water Trust or otherwise; and in connection therewith to enter into a financing agreement and/or security agreement with the Trust and otherwise to contract with the Trust and the Department of Environmental Protection with respect to such loan and for any federal or state aid available for the project or for the financing thereof; and that the Select Board, Department of Public Works or other appropriate local body or official is authorized to enter into a project regulatory agreement with the Department of Environmental Protection, to expend all funds available for the project; and that the Select Board is authorized to take any other action necessary to carry out this project, or take any other action relative thereto. PLANNING DEPARTMENT ARTICLE 18: Easement – Retaining Wall, 75 Long Pond Road To see if the Town will vote to authorize the Select Board to grant and convey a perpetual nonexclusive easement to Late Night, LLC for a retaining wall that is encroaching on and occupying town-owned land at 75 Long Pond Road, Plymouth, Massachusetts and further, for the purposes of maintaining and repairing over, across and under a portion of town-owned property at 75 Long Pond Road, Plymouth Massachusetts (the “Easement Area”), and known as Assessor’s Map 89, Parcel 089-000-34F-001 and shown on a plan on file with the Town Clerk, “Retaining Wall, 75 Long Pond Road”, or take any other action relative thereto. TOWN MANAGER ARTICLE 19: Easement – Traffic Signal, 75 Long Pond Road To see if the Town will vote to authorize the Select Board to acquire by gift, purchase, or eminent domain, and upon such terms and conditions as it deems appropriate, a perpetual non-exclusive easement, from Late Night, LLC for purposes of constructing, maintaining and repairing certain improvements including, but not limited to, the traffic signals over, across and under a portion of the property at 75 Long Pond Road, Plymouth, Massachusetts (the “Proposed Highway Easement”) and known as Assessor’s Map 89, Parcel 089-000-34F-001 and shown on a plan on file with the Town Clerk, “Traffic Signal, 75 Long Pond Road”, or take any other action relative thereto. TOWN MANAGER ARTICLE 20: WITHDRAWN ARTICLE 21: CPC Article – Reduce Borrowing – Jenney Pond Dredging To see if the Town will vote to revise the funding sources and thereby amend the vote taken under Article 16B of the 2022 Spring Annual Town Meeting for the restoration and rehabilitation of Jenney Pond, for Open Space and Recreation purposes, by reducing the amount to be borrowed by a sum of money and appropriating said sum of money from Fiscal Year 2027 Community Preservation Act revenues or transfer from Community Preservation available funds or reserves for such purposes, and take any other action relative thereto. Ch. 184, §§31-33; and to authorize the Select Board to enter into all agreements and execute any and all instruments as may be necessary on behalf of the Town to effect said restriction and related to the project, or take any other action relative thereto. text: COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS Worcester, ss. ZDZ6ff f.? 26 PM /: 47 SHr~ EWSf3 1J; •Y. t-1 t\ SS To a Constab le of the Town of Shrewsbury in the County of Worcester GREETINGS: In the name of the Commonwealth of Mas achusetts you are directed to notify and warn the inhab itants of Shrewsbury qualified to vote in elections and town affairs, to meet at the several designated polling places in their respective precincts in said Shrewsbury, to wit: Precinct 1 Richard D. Carney Municipal Office Building 100 Maple Avenue - Selectmen's Meeting Room Precinct 2 and 6 Shrewsbury Senior Center 98 Maple Avenue Precinct 3 Calvin Coolidge School 1 Florence Street Precinct 4 Scandinavian Athletic Club 438 Lake Street Precincts 5 and 10 Sewer and Water Department 209 South Street Precincts 7 and 8 Spring Street School 123 Spring Street Precinct 9 Fire Station #3 20 CenTech Boulevard on Tuesday, the fifth day of May A.D., 2026, then and there to act upon the following : To vote by ballot for the election of the following named Town Officers, to wit: TWO Select Board members to be elected for three years TWO School Committee members to be elected for three years THREE Trustees of Public Library to be elected for three years Representative Town Meeting Members for each precinct as follows: PRECINCT 1 EIGHT to be elected for 3 years PRECINCT 2 NINE to be elected for 3 years PRECINCT 3 SIX to be elected for 3 years TWO to be elected for 1 year (to fill vacancy) PRECINCT4 SEVEN to be elected for 3 years PRECINCT 5 EIGHT to be elected for 3 years PRECINCT 6 EIGHT be elected for 3 years TWO to be elected for 2 years (to fill vacancy) PRECINCT 7 EIGHT to be elected for 3 years PRECINCT 8 EIGHT to be elected for 3 years PRECINCT 9 EIGHT to be elected for 3 years PRECINCT 10 EIGHT to be elected for 3 years 2 GREETINGS: You are further hereby directed to notify and warn the said inhabitants of the Town of Shrewsbury to meet in the Oak Middle School Auditorium, 45 Oak Street, in said Shrewsbury on Monday, the eighteenth day of May, AD., 2026, at seven o'clock post meridian, (7:00 P.M.), at which time and place the following articles will be acted upon and determined exclusively by Town Meeting members, in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 553 of the Acts of 1953 and subject to the referendum provided for by section sixteen of said Act. ARTICLE 1 To see if the Town will vote to receive the reports of Town officers and committees and to act thereon, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 2 To see if the Town will vote to choose the trustees of the Wright and Harlow Charitable Fund, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 3 To see if the Town will vote to transfer a sum of money from available funds in the Treasury and appropriate said sum to various departmental appropriations for a prior fiscal year, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 4 To see if the Town will vote to transfer a sum of money from available funds in the Treasury and appropriate said sum to various departments for Fiscal Year 2026, or take any other action in relation thereto. 3 ARTICLE 5 To see if the Town will vote to raise such sums of money by tax or any other source available to the Town as may be deemed necessary to pay Town debts and charges and appropriate the same as they may see fit for the fisca l year beginning July 1, 2026, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 6 To see if the Town will vote to accept a sum of money from th e Municipal Light Plant CATV division and appropriate said sum for use of the Board of Assessors in offsetting the tax rate for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 7 To see if the Town will vote to accept a sum of money received from the Municipal Light Plant in lieu of taxes, and appropriate said sum for use of the Board of Assessors in offsetting the tax rate for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 8 To see if the Town will vote to transfer from available funds in the Treasury a sum of money for use of the Board of Assessors in offsetting the tax rate for the fiscal year beginning July J, 2026, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 9 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds in the Treasury a sum of money to operate the Municipal and Residential Solid Waste Collection, Processing and Disposal Services Enterprise, for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, or take any other action in relation thereto . 4 ARTICLE 10 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds in the Treasury a sum of money to fund the operation of the Sewer system, for the fiscal year beginning July l , 2026, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 11 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds in the Treasury a sum of money to operate the Water Services Enterprise, for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 12 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds in the Treasury a sum of money to operate the Stom1water Services Enterprise, for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 13 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds in the Treasury a sum of money to operate the Cable Television Public, Educational and Governmental Access Services Enterprise, for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, or take any other action in relation thereto . ARTICLE 14 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds in the Treasury a sum of money to pay the medical expenses of retired disabled police officers and firefighters , or take any other action in relation thereto. 5 ARTICLE 15 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds in the Treasury a sum of money to fund the Insurance Trust Fund, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 16 To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds in the Treasury a sum of money to fund the General Stabilization Account, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 17 To see if the Town will vote to set the annual spending limits for the revolving accounts established and set forth in Article 22 of the General Bylaws, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 18 To see if the Town will vote to accept a stm1 of money from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts in accordance with the provisions of the Chapter 90 local transportation aid funding program and transfer said funds to the Department of Pub Iic Works for the purposes of maintaining, repairing, improving and constructing town ways, sidewalks and drains and related eligible expenses, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 19 To see if the Town will vote to transfer a sum of money from the Sale of Cemetery Lots account to the Cemetery Division for the care, improvement, embellishment or enlargement of the Cemetery, or to take any other action in relation thereto. 6 ARTICLE 20 To see if the Town wil l vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from avai lable funds in the Treasury a sum of money for the purpose of funding water quality improvement projects and other initiatives for lakes, ponds, and waterways within the Town of Shrewsbury, or take any other action in relation thereto. ARTICLE 21 To see if the Town wi ll vote to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds in the Treasury a sum of money for counseling and educational services, or take any other action in relation thereto.
