TOWN ELECTION ... 64 CONSENT CALENDAR PROCEDURES & MOTION ... 65 APPENDIX A – Annual Report of Revolving Funds ... 66 APPENDIX B – Definitions of Commonly Used Terms at Town Meeting ... 67 APPENDIX C – Table of Motions ... 68 4 FINANCE COMMITTEE REPORT TO TOWN MEETING INTRODUCTION TO THE FINANCE COMMITTEE Every Town in Massachusetts with a property valuation of over $1 million is required by state law, MGL Ch. 39, Sect 16, to have a Finance Committee (FinCom) that shall “consider any or all municipal questions for the purpose of making reports or recommendations to the Town.” According to the Department of Local Services (DLS), the Finance Committee is “the official fiscal watchdog for a Town. Because it is difficult for all taxpayers to be completely informed about every aspect of a Town’s finances, Fincoms were established so a representative group of taxpayers could conduct a thorough review of municipal finance questions on behalf of all citizens.” With this in mind, the Fincom’s primary responsibility is advisory, to examine the budget and all other warrant articles and make recommendations to the voters on each article. It also administers the Reserve Fund ($80,000) to provide for urgent and unforeseen expenditures that might arise between Town meetings. Lastly, although it is not required in our Charter, the Finance Committee Annual Report provides the Voters with an overview of the Town’s financial condition. In Stow, the Moderator appoints five voting members and up to five associate members to the Finance Committee. Any voter registered in Stow is eligible to join. As of the publication date, there are five voting members and one associate members on the committee. Town Revenues Town revenues totaled $37,478,124 in FY25, a 2.53% increase from FY24, with property taxes continuing to dominate revenue generation for the town. The recent downward trend in tax rate has been offset by the continued increase in property values. The tax revenue collected for FY25 was $34,455,790. Local receipts were collected totaling $2,473,436, and State Aid was $548,898. Most notably, revenues from state aid were down sharply (-31%) from FY24. Town Expenditures The town continues to demonstrate a commitment to maintaining the budgetary targets supported at the annual Town Meeting. Expenditures for FY25 totaled $34,778,145, an increase of $2,430,091 (7.51%) compared to FY24. As is usual, these expenditures were dominated by assessments from our two local school districts, followed by municipal operating costs, and debt servicing. Town Savings Town savings (Free Cash plus the Stabilization Fund) are “rainy day” accounts that are built up during good times and drawn down in bad times. Free Cash comes from receiving more-thanbudget revenue (taxes, state aid, budget money left over from the prior year) and/or spending less than our voted budget. It is annually certified each year by the Department of Revenue (DOR). 5 Fiscal Year 2025 2024 2023 2022 2021 2020 Free Cash $2,075,156 $3,276,056 $1,876,404 $2,049,610 $2,385,510 $2,897,441 % of budget Stabilization fund 5.97% 10% 5.38% 6.18% 7.45% 8.87% % of budget $1,691,393 $1,413,559 $950,339 $739,085 $523,077 $520,971 4.86 4.19% 2.73% 2.23% 1.63% 1.59% Total 3,766,549.00 4,689,615.00 2,826,743.00 2,788,695.00 2,908,587.00 3,418,412.00 Once certified, free cash is available for appropriation throughout the fiscal year, to be spent for any lawful purpose. Every dollar of free cash appropriated as revenue in the FY25 budget is a dollar that does not need to be raised and appropriated through taxation. These savings are a necessity, not a luxury, and accumulate to build a targeted balance or used to fund the next year’s budget. In discussions with Standard and Poor’s leading up to our AAA rating approval, which was reaffirmed in October of 2025, the Town was encouraged to attempt to maintain a stored asset balance of between 5% and 10% of the overall budget (10.8%). Property Tax Rate and Property Valuations The information presented in the table below shows the trends in the tax rate, average single family home valuation and average single family tax bill. Stow’s tax rate rose slightly in FY25, while our average single family home valuation and tax bill had smaller year-over-year increases compared to FY24. The town’s FY2025 tax rate was certified at 17.42 or a 2.58% increase from FY24. FY25 $17.42 Tax Rate (Per $1,000) 2.58% YoY % Change $750,49 Avg single Family valuation $531,500 $556,907 $640,760 $736,526 5 1.86% YoY % Change 7.21% 4.78% 15.06% 14.95% Average Single Family tax $13,074 Bill $10,619 $10,893 $11,617 $12,499 4.4% YoY % Change 4.10% 2.58% 6.65% 7.59% FY21 FY22 FY23 $19.98 $19.56 $18.13 -3.06% -2.10% -7.31% FY24 $16.97 -6.30% Other Post Employment Benefits (OPEB) Other Post-Employment Benefits (or OPEB) are benefits (other than pensions) that U.S. state and local governments provide to their retired employees. This is a long-term financial commitment we make to the people responsible for supporting and maintaining our community. The Town has achieved our initial OPEB funding target of 20% of total liability. 6 Fiscal Year FY25 FY24 FY23 FY22 FY21 FY20 FY19 FY18 Current OPEB Liability OPEB Savings % Of Liability $2,195,196.00 22.91% $1,771,195.00 19.46% $1,389,340.00 14.96% $1,081,675.00 11.65% $822,807.00 8.86% $577,144.00 6.21% $329,296.00 3.55% $218,453.00 2.35% $9,580,357.00 Fiscal Year 2027 Proposed Budget Analysis Looking forward to the 2027 requested budget and comparing to the 2026 voter-approved budget, key highlights are as follows: ● Total revenue is estimated at $44,929,970 including unused levy capacity. The primary contributor to the revenue estimates is property tax. Of the $44.9M, approximately $40.5M is attributable to property tax, inclusive of the prop 2 ½ increase allowance. New growth revenue at is projected at $200,000, down 13.8% from FY26. A projected total FY27 levy limit revenue of $35,350,400 represents a 3.08% increase over FY26. ● Based on the initial indications from the State regarding State Aide Revenue, we are only estimating a small increase of 3.91% (~$20k). Continuing the trend of the past few years State contributions to cities and towns has remained relatively flat compared to revenue at the State level. ● Revenue from local receipts (motor vehicle excise tax, permit fees, license fees, etc) is projected to increase 5.95% in FY27. This number is conservative, as we expect Masters Academy to come online and several developments to break ground in FY27. ● The Town Administrator is proposing to use $1,402,375 of Free Cash in FY27, which will be applied to the following: o Transfer $300 into the Stabilization Fund; o Transfer $100k into the Capital Stabilization Fund; o Contribute $235k to the OBEP Trust Fund; o Use $867,375 to fund the Capital Plan ● We also expect to need a transfer on Town Meeting floor to cover the remainder of the snow & ice deficit. At this time, that figure is not known. Once we see what we’ll have for available General Fund funds, we’ll have a final deficit amount. ● FY2027 expenditures are dominated, as is typical, by the Nashoba school assessment at 58.29% of expenditures, followed by the municipal budget (including insurance) at 27.21%, municipal debt service at 7.89%, and the Minuteman assessment at 6.62%. As with all three towns in the Nashoba regional district, Stow’s educational expenses are a substantial portion of the total expenditures in any given year. As an aggregate, inclusive of debt servicing, Education accounts for 67% of the operating budget. 7 ● Total expenditure is expected to increase by 1.92% above FY26 spending. While the Nashoba assessment remains the largest line item, we are happy to report that the projected assessment increase of 2.93% by Nashoba was partially offset by a 7.02% reduction by Minuteman. The budget requests include a 5.94% increase in the municipal budget, a 50% reduction in capital expenses, and a 5% increase in special article expenditures. ● The net increase for the FY27 budget is 4.22% over the FY26. In the Fall of 2025, the Town Administrator put before Special Town Meeting an adjustment to the Wage & Classification Schedule for non-union employees. This proposal had the Finance Committee’s support and overwhelmingly passed Town Meeting. The wage increases in this budget are primarily a result of those changes with relatively little increase in department expenses. Stow continues to operate very conservatively, with limited nonessential expenses in our municipal budget. For FY27, the Select Board renegotiated the Town Administrator’s contract; as a result of the market rate for the TA position, an increase has been budgeted for. This increase will bring salary in line with the median. However, she will still be far below the median for total compensation in the region. This increase represents 1.76% of the municipal increase. While this increase may appear large, the Finance Committee acknowledges the impact and dedication of our current TA. As such, the Finance Committee supports this pay adjustment to bring the Town Administrator closer to the median market value for her position. Fiscal Year 2027 Special Articles – Raise & Appropriate Special articles have increased from $496,150 to $520,850 – an increase of less than 5%. Some highlights to the special articles are: ● A $30,000 (50%) reduction in the cost of operating the municipal water supply serving town-owned properties. ● $15,000 to digitally archive permanent records, including documents, plans, and permit information. Fiscal Year 2027 Capital Articles In the past, year-over-year capital expenditure was primarily by allocation of CPC funds. Omitting the CPC fund usage, significant contributors to the capital allocation are the town’s need to replace aging vehicles and critical infrastructure. We have benefited from the ability to maintain vehicles for extended periods, with highway equipment having service lifetimes upwards of 30 years. However, the combination of deferred replacements and drastically increased delivery timelines is forcing us to be more proactive with regards to key pieces of highway equipment and other municipal vehicles (police cruiser, ambulance, fire engines). As some vehicles are experiencing a 12 year backorder, we must appropriate funds and get in the replacement queue in order to ensure we are able to continue providing essential services. 8 In FY27, the Town administrator is Administrator is proposing we procure a number of vehicles through borrowing. This will allow us to sign a purchase order, but not hold up cash, while we wait one to two years for delivery. It will also allow us to repair aging infrastructure within the general fund budget, while budgeting for a principal and interest payment over a number of years and not all at once. Notably, the proposal includes this borrowing within the tax levy and not as debt exclusion. The remainder of the capital plan, as proposed, will be supported through appropriation from free cash and CPC funds. This diversified approach to funding our capital needs will be central to maintaining the financial health and critical infrastructure of Stow in FY27 and beyond. Conclusion Coupled with the growth in housing prices, the Town-wide valuation has grown faster than our costs (i.e. budget expenditures growth), allowing the Town to fund approved projects and capital items for the last several years. Moreover, the Town continues to maintain enough stored assets to benefit from low interest rates on borrowing due to our AAA rating. In addition, Stow has a certified excess levy capacity of approximately $1.62 million. As previously mentioned, this allows the town to borrow money at a more favorable rate. It is our opinion that this is a fair and accurate picture of the Town’s financial state. Whether you are pleased or displeased, the Finance Committee reminds everyone that Town Meeting directly controls the rate of growth of Town expenses. We encourage your participation. Respectfully submitted, Brian Patuto (Chair), Ross Perry (Member), Tom Farnsworth (Member), Angela Zhang (Member), Jeff Kimmelman (Member), John Mulroy (Associate Member) 9 TOWN ADMINISTRATOR’S FY27 BUDGET RECOMMENDATION LETTER Town of Stow Office of the Town Administrator Denise M. Dembkoski Town Administrator 380 Great Road Stow, MA 01775 Tel: 978-897-2927 townadministrator@stow-ma.gov To: Select Board, Finance Committee, and Stow Residents From: Denise M. Dembkoski, Town Administrator Re: FY27 Budget Recommendations Date: March 31, 2026 The Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27) Operating Budget process provided an opportunity for management to, once again, undertake an honest assessment of town functions to determine what is working and what changes are necessary. Some of the recommended changes contained within this memorandum will have cost implications for the FY27 budget, but unfortunately, they are unavoidable. We are facing large increases in facility work and health insurance. At the Special Town Meeting in October 2025, I presented changes to the Wage and Classification Schedule to eliminate the first four steps of the scale and add four steps to the higher end of the scale. This would cause those employees in the first four steps to be reclassified to what is the new Step 1 (originally step 5) and employees who had been maxed out at then Step 12, would be reclassified to Step 8 and have additional step increases available to them. These changes impacted 11 employees on the low end of the ranges. In addition, 7 employees, who were maxed out, and had not received a step increase in a few years, will now receive one. All other employees are handled as usual, either receiving their Step and/or COLA increase. This year, in addition to the 2% Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA), all employees in Grades 6 – 8, will be granted a step increase. Employees in Grades 1 to 5 will be given the 2% COLA, as their next step increase is not until next year (FY28). The only Collective Bargaining Contract that was up for June 30, 2026, is the Local 3262 Firefighters Association. I met with the Fire Union over the course of late Winter/early Spring, and we have finalized their contract, with all financial impacts included in my budget recommendation. During the negotiations, we determined that the members of the fire union were paid well below the median for area firefighters, so there is a base wage adjustment factored into the budget, to bring them up to competitive salaries. There are two non-union contracts also up for June 30, 2026. One is for the Police Lieutenant and the other is for my contract. Both contracts have been successfully renegotiated and ratified by the Select Board, with all financial implications included in the budget recommendation. 10 For the FY27 budget, here are some key changes: The majority of the increases are the implementation of the new Salary Classification Plan, with many being the pay adjustments and 11 employees, who now receive a step increase. We had a number of employees retire over the last year, and were able to adjust the pay to a lower, but still competitive wage for many of those positions, saving money

Large Accessory Dwelling Unit (LADU) — An ADU that does not qualify as a Protected Use ADU, with a maximum gross floor area of 1,200 s.f. text: TOWN OF TOPSFIELD MASSACHUSETTS Annual and Special Town Meeting Warrants TOWN MEETING TUESDAY, MAY 5, 2026 Masconomet Regional School High School Auditorium 20 Endicott Road Boxford, MA Topsfield FY 2027 letter from the Finance Committee March 31,2026 Dear Fellow Residents, We thank the Town and School employees for their continuing dedication to providing essential services to our residents. It is through their efforts that Topsfield continues to be a wonderful town to live in. In addition, it takes significant commitment from all the volunteers who support and improve our town. We encourage all town residents to actively participate in town government, whether attending meetings, listening sessions, or volunteering for Boards and Committees. Municipal budgets across the Commonwealth are facing pressure from increased costs and limited state funding. Topsfield’s budget will continue to be a challenge in coming years, requiring difficult discussions and decisions about the services Topsfield provides and the taxes it collects to pay for the services. Your involvement early and often allows you to influence the directions our town takes. FY2027 Financial Overview The Finance Committee’s FY2027 Budget Process began in November 2025, when we issued budget guidelines for Town Government, Elementary School, Masconomet and Essex Tech, based on revenues projected to balance their budgets within the confines of Proposition 2 %. We track the Town, Elementary School, Masconomet, and Essex Tech budgets separately and hold each to the guideline for their budget. Those responsible for planning budgets may request an override when they determine that balanced budget guidelines are insufficient to fund operations. The Select Board decided to include two overrides in this year’s warrant as detailed below. The Finance Committee’s recommendations on all Warrant articles are subject to your approval at the Annual Town Meeting, and contingent on passage at the Town Election on May 7. Please visit the Town Meeting webpage at Topsfield- ma.gov to review The FY27 Warrant Articles Vote Summary, which reports the Finance Committee’s considerations and recommendations for each warrant article. Wages, health insurance, and pension benefits are growing at rates far greater than 2-1/2% and continue to be the main drivers of budget increases. The Finance Committee requests that town and education officials continue to seek ways to reduce these increases by always considering total compensation inclusive of current and future benefits. Topsfield FY 2027 letter from the Finance Committee March 31,2026 Compound Annual Growth Rate FY2022-2027 Health insurance 3 4 | 9.3% Pensions 7.0% Elementary (I «1 | I I | Masco/Essex NS i Tate : 5 5.9% - I 1 i Town Govt (2.9% I 0% 1% 2% ! 3% a% 5% ; 6% 7% 8% 9% 10% ! MA Prop Total Budget 2.5% 5.4% *Health Insurance and Pensions detailed here are for Town and Elementary expenses. Masco/Essex NS includes their Health Insurance and Pensions in their operating budget. Free Cash This year we have $3,800,000 in free cash. It should be emphasized that $1.1 million of the Free Cash is a result of one-time events that will not reoccur. A significant part of these funds (over $400,000) will be used to rebuild the General and Capital stabilizations Funds as shown in Articles 50, 515, FY2027 Operating Budget (Article 3" only: Town & Elementary School + Town Operating Budget (Article 3") The Town budget increase is driven primarily by wages, health insurance (which includes town and elementary employees), and pension obligations. Thanks to the public’s efforts to reduce the waste stream, our variable costs for rubbish collection are improving. Notable items in the Town portion of Article 3": e Health Insurance increase for Town and Elementary by $364,805 (12.9%) e Pension costs increased $144,125 (7.73%) Topsfield FY 2027 letter from the Finance Committee March 31,2026 e The salary & wages of the town include an increase of $240,789 (4.08%), which includes retro pay for fire and police (FY25,26) contracts, the addition of a fulltime firefighter and part time planner. e Snow and Ice deficit for FY2026 of $151,000. Due to this growth the Town is requesting an override of $317,084. Elementary Schools (Article 3") After significant effort and collaboration with the Town, Select Board, and Finance Committee, the Topsfield Elementary School Committee has presented a budget that meets the guidelines of the Finance Committee of $12,614,497, an increase of (2.25%) and therefore no override is requested for the Elementary School. The Finance Committee recommends Positive Action on the Article 3" Budget, appearing as Motions A and B on the Warrant. Masconomet Budget (Article 5") The Masconomet total operating budget increases are driven by Salaries and Health Insurance. The school committee made significant structural changes to better align the budget with current enrollment, including a net reduction of 10 FTEs. Topsfield’s contribution grew 2.6%, which is in line with the other towns. Article Sth results in a total $11,251,147 assessment to Topsfield including an override request of $140,316. Boxford and Middleton will not require an override and will almost certainly approve their share. The Regional Agreement will oblige Topsfield to fund this over guideline increase. The Finance Committee recommends positive action. Essex North Shore Agricultural and Technical School District (Article 6") The total operating budget services 17 communities. Topsfield’s share of the Operating Budget is calculated based on State mandated The total operating budget increased by 4.5% or $1,856,622 to $43,134,188, Topsfield’s share is calculated based on State mandated Net School Spending requirements and its share of the District’s enrollment. Topsfield’s share of the operating budget increased by 20.8% or $104,827, due to budget increases and three additional Topsfield students. The enrollment policy was changed to a lottery, which increased Topsfield’s minimum acceptances from 7 to 15 students, which will have a significant impact on the Essex North Shore budgets for FY28 and beyond. The overrides must pass at Town Meeting and at the ballot on Thursday May 7". Ballot Question 2, Secondary Education Override, totals $233,788 of which $93,472 supports Essex North Shore and $140,316 supports Masconomet. Topsfield FY 2027 letter from the Finance Committee March 31,2026 FY2027 Other Appropriations Water Enterprise Article 4" The Water Enterprise, providing water to many Topsfield residents, has an overall budget of $2,604,390, an increase of 0.8%. The budget is funded by water rate payers. The Finance Committee recommends positive action Additional investments of $175,000 are included in articles 30th, 31st, and 32nd under consent agenda three. These articles are funded by retained earnings. The Finance Committee recommends positive action. Consent Agendas for Capital and One-Time Purchases The Finance Committee worked with the Town Administration and departments/boards on prioritizing funding for capital and one-time purchases. Careful deliberations sought to manage the purchases to essential items in order to limit the impact on Town finances. At Town Meeting our Town Moderator will guide voters through a series of Consent Agendas. e Consent Agenda One Articles 7"to 14" - Articles 7" and 8" require no funding; Articles 9"-14" continue to be funded with Free Cash. Total Appropriation of $208,101. The Finance Committee recommends positive action on all articles. ¢ Consent Agenda Two Articles 15" to 29" fund Capital Equipment. Total Appropriations $1,019,000, of which $905,000 is funded with Free Cash, $105,000 from Ambulance Stabilization Fund, and $9,000 from Water Enterprise Fund Retained Earnings. o The Finance Committee recommends positive action on Articles 15th-17th, 19th- 23rd, 25th-29", and no action on Articles 18" and 24", A consent agenda’s purpose is to allow the Finance Committee’s recommendation under these articles to be acted upon in a single vote. Any voter may raise an objection to the inclusion of any article(s), requesting they be debated, and voted separately from the consent. The Finance Committee’s recommendations to which no objection has been made will then be offered for acceptance by the Town Meeting in a single vote without debate. The Finance Committee has recommended no action on the following capital purchase warrant articles: 18" Police Command Vehicle — This purchase was originally in the Town’s capital plan for FY28. The current vehicle continues to serve its purpose and the purchase could be delayed. 24* Multi-Use Lift Hook Medium Duty Truck — While we see the utility and value in this choice of truck, the current truck continues to fill its function as a snowplow and salt spreader.

title: 2026 Special Town Meeting Warrant
text: TOWN OF TOPSFIELD WARRANT FOR 2026 SPECIAL TOWN MEETING Essex, ss. To the Constable of the Town of Topsfield, in said County, In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are directed to notify the inhabitants of the Town of Topsfield, qualified to vote in elections and in Town affairs, to meet at the MASCONOMET REGIONAL SCHOOL HIGH SCHOOL AUDITORIUM 20 ENDICOTT ROAD BOXFORD MA in Boxford, on Tuesday, the fifth day of May, 2026, at half past seven in the evening (7:30 PM) then and there to act on the following articles: ARTICLE FIRST: REPORTS To hear all reports that may legally come before the meeting. ARTICLE SECOND: PRIOR YEAR BILLS To see if the Town will vote to transfer from available funds a sum of money to pay any outstanding bills contracted prior to July 1, 2025. Recommendation pending further review. ARTICLE THIRD: FISCAL YEAR 2026 BUDGET TRANSFERS To see if the Town will vote to transfer from the unexpended balance of certain accounts, and/or from available funds, and appropriate said funds to certain other accounts to pay certain expenses for the 2026 fiscal year, or take any other action relative thereto. Recommendation pending further review. Page 1 of 3 ARTICLE FOURTH: FISCAL YEAR 2026 SNOW AND ICE DEFICIT To see if the Town will vote to raise and assess, or transfer from available funds, and appropriate a sum of money to be expended by the Select Board to fund part of the Fiscal Year 2026 Snow and Ice deficit, including all incidental and related expenses, or take any other action relative thereto. Recommended that the Town vote to transfer the sum of $35,000 from Overlay Surplus, and appropriate from Free Cash the sum of $52,916, to be expended by the Select Board to fund part of the Fiscal Year 2026 Snow and Ice deficit, including all incidental and related expenses. This article would provide the necessary funds, from certified Overlay Surplus and Free Cash, to pay for a portion of snow and ice removal overages that occurred this past winter (calendar 2025/26). These overages were due to the timing, length and significance of storms this past season. This appropriation will cover a portion of the deficit, the remaining deficit balance is being funded through the proposed appropriation in Article Third of the 2026 Annual Town Meeting warrant and a proposed 2026 fiscal year budget transfer in the above Article Third of this 2026 Special Town Meeting warrant. ARTICLE FIFTH: HEALTH INSURANCE PREMIUMS RECONCILIATION To see if the Town will vote to raise and assess, or transfer from available funds, and appropriate a sum of money to be expended by the Select Board to fund the non-recoverable Health Insurance Premiums from Town and School employees, including all incidental and related expenses, or take any other action relative thereto. Recommended that the Town vote to transfer the sum of $27,878 from Overlay Surplus, to be expended by the Select Board to fund the non-recoverable Health Insurance Premiums from Town and School employees, including all incidental and related expenses. This article would allow the Town to make an accounting adjustment, utilizing certified Overlay Surplus, to address the outstanding liability associated with employee Health Insurance that was incorrectly withheld from multiple employees when they were onboarded or when changes were made to their health insurance plans. An internal audit was performed in 2020 to confirm whether current and former employees’ withholdings for the initial month of coverage was correctly billed for each new employee over the past 20 years. The audit determined that some employees’ withholdings were incorrect during the onboarding period and when changes were made to an employee’s insurance plan. The Town worked with active employees and was able to recover a substantial amount of the balances owed to the Town. However due to many of the employees no longer being employed, the Town was not able to collect these funds. As a result, the accounting adjustment needs to be made. Since the time of the audit employees’ withholdings have been accounted for accurately. *** You are directed to serve this Warrant by posting attested copies thereof, one at the Post Office, one at the Town Hall, and one at each of the Public Meeting Houses in said Town, seven days at least before time for holding the election portion of said meeting. Hereof fail not, and make due return of this Warrant, with your doing thereon, to the Town Clerk, at the time and place of meeting as aforesaid. Given under our hands this Thirty-First day of March in the year two thousand and twenty-six. Page 2 of 3 TOWN OF TOPSFIELD SELECT BOARD ___ Rafael N. McDonald, Chair ___ Michelle M. text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 6th Article Name: Essex North Shore agricultural and Technical School District Finance Committee Liaison: Heidi Fox Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Essex North Shore Agricultural and Technical School (ENSATS) Committee Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to raise, assess and appropriate the sum of $516,025 for a portion of the Town’s share of the Fiscal Year 2027 Essex North Shore Agricultural and Technical School District Gross Budget assessment and the additional sum of $93,472 to fully fund the amount assessed to the Town under the Fiscal 2027 Essex North Shore Agricultural and Technical School District Gross Budget assessment, provided, however, that such additional appropriation shall be expressly contingent upon approval by the voters at an election of a Proposition 2 ½ override, so called, pursuant to G.L. c. 59, § 21C(g); and, further, to acknowledge that if such override is passed at the election, the Town will have approved the Essex North Shore Agricultural and Technical School District FY2027 total Gross Budget in the amount of $43,134,188. The additional appropriation of $93,472 is contingent on the passage of Ballot Question Two at the Annual Town Election on May 7. If the Prop 2-1/2 ballot question passes, Topsfield will have appropriated its full assessment of the proposed budget. Please note that Question Two combines the $140,316 Masco override with the $93,472 ENSATS override. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION Yes 7 No 0 Abstain 0 Reasoning: In Favor: Topsfield is one of 17 communities that appropriate their full assessment in order to approve the proposed full budget of $43,134,188. Ch70 requires that each community contribute a Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details minimum to the district’s operating budget. Our additional 3 pupils increased our required contribution to the Operating Budget (7.8% per pupil). The request for an override is necessary to fully fund FY27’s assessment and increase levy capacity to support an anticipated 8-student increase in FY28. Opposed: N/A

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 3 - General Operating Budget
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 3rd Article Name: General Operating Budget Finance Committee Liaison: Michael Koniares Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Town Administrator Warrant Motion: Motion A – Base Budget Appropriation. Recommended that the Town vote to appropriate the sum of $28,331,186 for elementary schools, highways, public safety and other Town expenses, and fix the annual salary and compensation of all elected officers from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and determine the manner of expending the same, and to meet said appropriation, in addition to the amount of $102,432 transferred for such purposes under Article Second, to transfer the sum of $10,000 from Overlay Surplus, and raise and assess the sum of $28,218,754. Description of Warrant: Motion A would approve the Base Budget Appropriation of the Fiscal Year 2027 General Operating Budget of $28,331,186 that is funded by a transfer of $102,432 from Article Second, a transfer from Overlay Surplus of $10,000, plus assessed taxes of $28,218,754 which tax amount is within the Town’s Proposition 2 ½ levy limit. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 7-0 Reasoning: In Favor: Motion A provides funding for the Town within both the Proposition 2 ½ levy limit and the Finance Committee guideline. Opposed: N/A. Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Warrant Motion: Motion B – Contingency Appropriation. Recommended that the Town vote to raise, assess and appropriate an additional sum of $317,084 to fully fund the additional portion of the proposed Fiscal Year 2027 General Operating budget, as set forth in the row labeled “Article 3, Motion B” in Attachment A, provided, however, that such additional appropriation shall be expressly contingent upon approval by the voters at an election of a Proposition 2 ½ override, so-called, pursuant to G.L. c. 59, § 21C(g). Description of Warrant: Motion B would approve an additional Contingency Appropriation of $317,084 for general operations. The additional Contingency Appropriation is primarily related to health insurance and pension costs in the Fiscal Year 2027 General Operating Budget. Since Fiscal Year 2024 health insurance costs for the town and schools have increased by $991,019 (40.4%) and pensions have increased by $284,361 (16.5%), much faster than the Town’s levy capacity. The Town is obligated by Massachusetts General Law to offer health insurance and provide pensions to employees. By funding the additional Contingency Appropriation, it will allow the Town to meet this statutory obligation without reducing the level of operational services provided to the community. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 4-2 Reasoning: In Favor: The additional appropriation in Motion B is necessary in order for the Town to meet its long term obligations such as health insurance and pensions while maintaining level service. Opposed: Article 3, B “contingency appropriation”, is a Town override for $317,000, resulting in a total Town budget (everything but schools) increase of $925,480 (6.15% including health insurance and pension increases). The expanded budget includes the addition of one and a half (1 ½) new employees this year: a fulltime fire fighter and a part time planner. Further, the dissenting opinion is that these positions are not essential: (1) The Fire Department has 8 full-time firefighters; this allows for 2 people to be in the station 24/7. At this point the Fire Department should define and get agreement on the long-term plans for TFD before asking for extra personnel. Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details (2) The planner position is a new position which is meant to support some Planning Board and the Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA) efforts but also to support the town’s strategic planning needs. In contrast, MASCO made the very difficult decision to reduce employees by 10 in order to moderate the increase in their budget. Additional Concerns The override also includes $57,000 for the snow and ice budget that was overspent due to the unusual winter weather. This is a one-time event that should be covered by one-time funds such as free cash. By adding this to the override it will permanently increase the levy limit by $57,000. Note: The Elementary School budget is NOT contingent on passage of article 3rd, motion 3B and override ballot Question One. They have not requested an override for FY 2027.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 5 - Masconomet Regional School District Assessment
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 5th Article Name: Masconomet Regional School District Operating Assessment Finance Committee Liaison: Heidi Fox Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Masconomet Regional School Committee Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to raise, assess and appropriate the sum of $11,110,831 to fund a portion of the Town’s share of the Fiscal Year 2027 Masconomet Regional School District Operating Assessment and the additional sum of $140,316 to fully fund the remaining portion of the Town’s share of the Fiscal 2027 Masconomet Regional School District Operating Assessment, provided, however, that such additional appropriation shall be expressly contingent upon approval by the voters at an election of a Proposition 2 ½ override, so called, pursuant to G.L. c. 59, § 21C(g); and, further, to acknowledge that if such override is passed at the election, the Town will have approved the Masconomet Regional School District FY2027 proposed budget in the requested amount of $44,951,409. If the Prop 2-1/2 ballot question passes, Topsfield will have appropriated its full assessment of the proposed budget. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION Yes 6 No 0 Abstain 1 Reasoning: In Favor: The Masconoment Administration and School Committee made structural cuts including reductions of 10 postions to keep their FY27 budget to the Tri-Town coordinated guideline of 2.5% increase. Topsfield anticipated an override to fund that portion of our assessment in excess of a 2.25% due to continued enrollment swings and maintenance needs. It is Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details expected that Middleton and Boxford will not require an override to approve their full assessments, which will obligate Topsfield to fund its full assessment. We recommend fully funding Topsfield’s assessment of $11,251,147. Opposed: N/A

The Abstention reflects that concern.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 38 - Accepted Roads
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 38th Article Name: Accepted Roads Finance Committee Liaison: Heidi Fox Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Highway/Select Board Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to accept as public ways, Aaron Drive, Beech Place, Deer Run, Evergreen Lane, Hickory Lane, Pearl Way, Pemberton Road, Pheasant Lane, Ruby Circle, and School Avenue, as set forth in this Article Thirty-Eighth in the warrant. Description of Warrant: These roads are not currently in the MA Road Inventory as public ways, and involved extensive research by Hwy Dept to identify the locations, boundaries and measurements for acceptance of these roads, and record the “lane miles” for which Ch90 funds can be filed. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION Yes 7 No 0 Abstain 0 Reasoning: In Favor: The Highway Department has provided snow plowing and minor repairs on these roads but cannot perform extensive repairs and apply for Ch90 funding unless the roads are accepted as public ways. It is estimated that Topsfield loses approximately $25K per year because we are not getting credit for these lane miles. Opposed: N/A

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 39 - Mile Brook Bridge New Highway Layout and Easement Acceptance
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 39th Article Name: Perkins Row/Mile Brook Bridge Project Finance Committee Liaison: Heidi Fox Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Select Board/Town Adminstration Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to approve Article Thirty-Eighth as printed in the warrant. Description of Warrant: The construction to replace the failing 1905-built bridge is scheduled for the summer of 2027. As part of the work, the state requires that the Town obtain temporary construction and permanent rights to land abutting the bridge. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION Yes 7 No 0 Abstain 0 Reasoning: In Favor: There are two properties that abut the bridge, one owned by the Town and the other by MA Audubon. The State is paying for the design and construction of the bridge. If this article is not approved, the state funding would be deferred and replacement of the bridge may not start as scheduled. Opposed: N/A

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 31 - Water SCADA System Upgrade
text: Finance Committee FY2026 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 31st Article Name: Water: SCADA Sytem Upgrades (Supervisory Control And Data Acquistion) Finance Committee Liaison: Tom Watkins Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Water Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to transfer and appropriate from Water Enterprise Fund retained Earnings the sum of $75,000 to be expended by the Select Board, to fund the purchase and installation of a new SCADA system for the water treatment plant, including all incidental or related expenses. Description of Warrant: This article utilizes Retained Earnings from the Town’s Water Enterprise Fund to fund the replacement of the main programmable logic controller that operates the SCADA system. The current system was last updated in 2010 and needs to be replaced before it fails. This funding request will also improve the physical and cyber-security of the SCADA system. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION The Finance Committee recommends positive action (vote 7-0) Reasoning: In Favor: The current system is old and obsolete, no longer supported and is in danger of failing. Therefore replacement is necessary. The SCADA is the core management system for the water system. This will also improve the cyber-security system of the SCADA system. Opposed: Keep the funds in Retained Earnings in order to fund another capital project request

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 32 - Water Large Item Repair Fund
text: Finance Committee FY2026 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 32nd Article Name: Water: Large Item Repair Fund Finance Committee Liaison: Tom Watkins Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Water Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to transfer and appropriate from Water Enterprise Fund Retained Earnings the sum of $50,000 to be expended by the Select Board, to fund water treatment plant infrastructure repairs, including all incidental or related expenses. Description of Warrant: This article utilizes Retained Earnings from the Town’s Water Enterprise Fund and will be used to repair major system components such as raw water pumps, process transfer pumps, backwash pumps and finished water pumps as needed. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION The Finance Committee recommends positive action (vote 7-0) Reasoning: In Favor: These major repairs are needed in order to maintain the operation of the water treatment plant, most notably the working condition of a variety of pumps. These funds will support general maintenance needs outside of the Water Department’s Operational Budget. Opposed: Keep the funds in Retained Earnings in order to fund another capital project request

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 33 - Amend Zoning Bylaw Modify Accessory Dwelling Unit Bylaw
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 33rd Article Name: Amend Zoning Bylaw: Modify Accessory Dwelling Unit Bylaw Finance Committee Liaison: Heidi Fox Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Planning Board Warrant Motion: Recommended the Town vote to amend the Topsfield Zoning Bylaw, Article VII Special Regulations, Section 7.03 Accessory Dwelling Unit, and amend Article I, Definitions, as set forth in this Article Thirty-Third in the warrant. Description of Warrant: The ADU bylaw was passed at 2025 ATM. The language was reviewed by MA Attorney General’s office. This article refines the language in Article I.03 Definitions, and Article 7.03 Section D.v. to comply with State’s review. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION Yes 7 No 0 Abstain 0 Reasoning: In Favor: The Finance Committee agrees with the recommendation of the Planning Board adopting state language. Opposed: N/A

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 43 - Special act to allow continued employment of the police chief
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 43rd Article Name: Home rule petition: to extend employment of the police chief Finance Committee Liaison: David Larson Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Police Department Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to authorize the Select Board to file special legislation with the General Court allowing the Town to continue to employ the Police Chief Neal Hovey when he has reached the statutory age of retirement, in the form set forth in this Article Forty-Third of the warrant; provided, however, that the General Court shall be authorized to make changes of form only to the bill without the approval of the Select Board and, further, to authorize the Select Board to approve such changes as are within the public purposes of the petition. Description of Warrant: The Police chief, Neal Hovey, will reach the mandatory retirement age of 65 in about one year. This article would allow the Town to petition the state to permit the Chief to work 3 additional years to age 68. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 6-1 Reasoning: In Favor: This would permit a request to the state to grant an exception to the mandatory retirement age for Police Chief Hovey Opposed: This would delay the towns option to promote the existing Captain and then streamline the police department command structure.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 44 - Citizens Petition Home Rule Petition for Ban of SGARS
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 44th Article Name: Citizen Petition: Home Rule Petition for Restriction on Reodenticides Finance Committee Liaison: Heidi Fox Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Citizen Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to approve the Citizen Petition, as set forth in this Article Forty-Fourth in the warrant. Description of Warrant: The article appears on the warrant as submitted with the requisite number of signatures. If approved at ATM, Topsfield will officially request that the Legislature give local officials the authority to ban the use of second-generation anticoagulant rodenticides (SGARS). If the Legislature grants the home rule petition, the Town will have to write a bylaw to ban the use of SGARS on private property, and submit for vote at future ATM. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION Yes 6 No 1 Abstain 0 Reasoning: In Favor: Topsfield has already banned the use of SGARS on municipal property. There are 21 other communities that have requested home rule petitions, designed to put pressure on the Legislature to ban SGARS at the state level. Legislation has moved out of the MA House Committee on Environment and Natural Resources. If state legislation is passed the home rule petition would be null and void. Private property owners can request that professional exterminators use alternative methods to eliminate rodents, as the poisons pose a danger to natural predators and scavengers. Opposed: Banning the chemicals eliminates an option for eliminating pests.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 45 - Masconomet REgional School Capital Debt Authorization
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: Article 45th Article Name: Masconomet Regional School District Capital Debt Authorization Finance Committee Liaison: Heidi Fox Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Masconomet Regional School District Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town hereby approves the $1,738,652 borrowing, consisting of $698,938 for Masconomet High School and $1,039,714 for Masconomet Middle School, authorized by the Masconomet Regional District School Committee (the “District”), for the purpose of paying feasibility study and schematic design costs related to a potential Accelerated Repair Project involving replacement of the roof and conversion of the HVAC system to heat pumps at Masconomet Middle School, located at 20 Endicott Rd in Boxford, MA, and replacement of the roof and conversion of the HVAC system to heat pumps at Masconomet High School, located at 20 Endicott Rd. in Boxford, MA, including the payment of all costs incidental or related thereto (the “Project”), which proposed repair project would materially extend the useful life of the school and preserve an asset that otherwise is capable of supporting the required educational program, and for which the District may be eligible for a school construction grant from the Massachusetts School Building Authority (the “MSBA”), said amount to be expended at the direction of the Masconomet School Committee; that the Town acknowledges that the MSBA’s grant program is a non-entitlement, discretionary program based on need, as determined by the MSBA, and any Project costs the District incurs in excess of any grant approved by and received from the MSBA shall be the sole responsibility of the District and its member municipalities; provided that the approval of the District’s borrowing by this vote shall be subject to and contingent upon an affirmative vote of the Town to exempt its allocable share of the amounts required for the payment of interest and principal on said borrowing from the limitations on taxes imposed by M.G.L. Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details 59, Section 21C(k) (Proposition 2 ½); and that the amount of borrowing authorized by the District shall be reduced by any grant amount set forth in the Project Funding Agreement that may be executed between the District and the MSBA. Description of Warrant: This article requests approval of $1,738,652 of debt, authorized by the MRDSC, to fund the initial Schematic Design Phase of “Roof/HVAC Project.” Ballot Question Three requests that Topsfield’s assessment of the future debt be excluded from the Prop 2-1/2 tax levy limitations. This is the first phase of a Roof/HVAC Project estimated to cost in excess of $66 million, funding for which will be requested for approval at future Town Meetings. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION Yes 4 No 2 Abstain 0 Reasoning: In Favor: This project has been accepted into the Massachussets School Building Authority’s (MSBA) Accelerated Repair Program, which will qualify the MRSD for reimbursement of approximately 40% of the costs of the “Roof/HVAC Project.” Approval of this funding by all three towns in the MRSD will allow for the hiring of an Owner’s Project Manager (OPM) and completion of schematic designs, which is a pre-requesite for moving forward with additional funding for construction. Opposed: There were concerns about the added cost to comply with MSBA’s conditions that heat pump technology and airconditioning be part of the repairs, and that those added costs may be greater than the state grants.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 47 - Special Education Stablization Fund
text: Finance Committee FY2026 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 47 Article Name: SPECIAL EDUCATION STABILIZATION FUND Finance Committee Liaison: Catherine Hodges Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Elementary School Committee Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to transfer and appropriate from Free Cash the sum of $75,000 to the Special Education Stabilization Fund. Description of Warrant: The Special Education Stabilization Fund was established in 2024 for the purpose of setting aside funds annually to address the unpredictability of the year-to-year special education costs in the elementary schools by supplementing the special education costs and the annual budget through the Special Education Stabilization Fund. Such appropriation may be funded with Free Cash, equal to the savings realized in the prior year school’s actual costs compared with their allocated budget, which are turned back to the Town. Appropriations to such fund remain in the fund year-to-year until appropriated by Town Meeting for the purpose of the fund. Appropriation of monies into the Special Education Stabilization Fund requires a majority vote of Town Meeting. Finance Committee Recommendation: POSITIVE ACTION Finance Committee Vote: No 0 Yes 7 Abstain 0 Reasoning: In Favor: The Finance Committee is committed to fund this as the school returned an equivalent amount of unspent funds to the town last year. We felt very strongly about honoring this commitment. Opposed: N/A

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 48 - Special Education Reserve Fund
text: Finance Committee FY2026 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 48 Article Name: SPECIAL EDUCATION RESERVE FUND Finance Committee Liaison: Catherine Hodges Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Elementary School Committee Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to transfer and appropriate from Free Cash the sum of $75,000 to the Special Education Reserve Fund. Description of Warrant: The Special Education Reserve Fund was established in 2019 for the purpose of setting aside funds periodically to address the unpredictability of during a year special education costs in the elementary schools, such as unanticipated or unbudgeted special education costs, out of district tuition, and/or special education transportation by supplementing the special education costs and the annual budget through the Special Education Reserve Fund. Such appropriation may be funded with Free Cash, equal to the savings realized in the prior year school’s actual costs compared with their allocated budget, which are turned back to the Town. Appropriations to such fund remain in the fund year-to-year until appropriated jointly by the Topsfield School Committee and Topsfield Select Board for the purpose of the fund. The balance of the Special Education Reserve Fund cannot exceed 2% of annual net school spending of the school district. Appropriation of monies into the Special Education Reserve Fund requires a majority vote of Town Meeting. Finance Committee Recommendation: POSITIVE ACTION Finance Committee Vote: No 0 Yes 7 Abstain 0 Reasoning: In Favor: The Finance Committee is committed to fund this as the school returned an equal amount of unspent funds to the town last year. We felt very strongly about honoring this commitment. Finance Committee FY2026 Warrant Vote Details Opposed: N/A

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 49 - Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) Trust Fund
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 49th Article Name: Other Post-Employment Benefits (“OPEB”) Trust Fund Finance Committee Liaison: Michael Koniares Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Town Treasurer Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to transfer and appropriate from Free Cash the sum of $440,000 to the Other Post-Employment Benefits Liability Trust Fund. Description of Warrant: This article allows the Town to continue to fund its OPEB liability by depositing funds in the OPEB Trust. The Town’s Financial Policies recommend increasing the funding amount by $20,000 each year until the annual funding amount reaches $500,000 after which the funding amount will remain at $500,000 annually until the Trust is fully funded. OPEB liabilities relate primarily to funding healthcare for retirees. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 7-0 Reasoning: In Favor: This warrant recommendation is contistent with the Town’s Financial Policies and demonstrates sound fiscal management in continuing to apply funds towards a large liability. Opposed: Some or all of these funds could be used to fund current needs and the Town could satisfy the OPEB liability over a longer time period.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 50 - Capital Stabilization Fund
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 50th Article Name: Capital Stabilization Fund Finance Committee Liaison: Michael Koniares Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Town Administrator/Accounting Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to transfer and appropriate from Free Cash the sum of $57,876 to the Capital Stabilization Fund. Description of Warrant: The Capital Stabilization Fund was established for the purpose of setting aside funds annually to address long term capital needs. Appropriations to such fund remain in the fund from year to year until appropriated by a majority vote of Town Meeting for any legal purpose consistent with the purpose of the fund. Like the General Stabilization Fund, appropriation of monies into the Capital Stabilization Fund requires a majority vote of Town Meeting. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 7-0 Reasoning: In Favor: Consistent with sound financial management, the Town is placing currently available Free Cash into a designated fund for future use. The amount is equal to the amount withdrawn from the Fund at last year’s Town Meeting when less Free Cash was available for use. Opposed: Some or all of these funds could be used to fund current needs. Discussion if the Capital Stabilization Fund is the optimal reserve fund for future needs.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 41 - Special Legislation Authorizing Print-Free Digital Legal Notices
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 41st Article Name: Home Rule Petition: Authorizing Print-Free Digital Legal Notices Finance Committee Liaison: Che Elwell Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Town / Select Board Warrant Motion: To see if the Town will vote to authorize the Select Board to file a Home Rule Petition with the General Court for special legislation, as set forth below, allowing the Town to satisfy state and local legal notice publication requirements by posting/publishing in local digital newspapers, print media, or both, rather than in traditional newspapers; Recommended that the Town vote to authorize the Select Board to petition the General Court for special legislation to allow the Town to satisfy requirements for publication of legal notices by allowing the publication of notices in local digital newspapers, print media, or both, all as set forth in this Article Forty-First in the warrant. Description of Warrant: This article would allow the Select Board to petition the General Court for a special act that would provide the Town with greater flexibility relative to satisfying statutory notice publication requirements, and allow the Town to avoid the related publication expenses. However, the Town would continue to be subject to all statutory timing requirements for such notices. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 7-0 Reasoning: In Favor: If the state grants the petition, we would be able to more efficiently and economically provide notifications in digital formats Opposed: There may be some people who prefer, or more easily can access the print notifications.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 42 - Local Acceptance State Prudent Investor Act
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 42nd Article Name: Local Acceptance: State Prudent Investor Act Finance Committee Liaison: Michael Koniares Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Town Treasurer Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to accept the provisions of G.L. c. 44, §54(b) to allow Town trust funds to be invested in accordance with G.L. c. 203C, the Prudent Investor Act. Description of Warrant: This article allows the Treasurer to utilize the Prudent Investor Act, as defined in G.L. c. 203C, to optimize returns on investments of trust funds. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 7-0 Reasoning: In Favor: This is an opportunity to align the Town’s investment policy with modern investment principles, including seeking higher returns for trust fund assets. Opposed: Discussed the importance of making sure any investment changes appropriately consider risk.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 51 - General Stabilization Fund
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 51st Article Name: General Stabilization Fund Finance Committee Liaison: Michael Koniares Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Town Administrator/Accounting Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to transfer and appropriate from Free Cash the sum of $344,565 to the General Stabilization Fund. Description of Warrant: The General Stabilization Fund is sometimes called the “rainy day fund” and provides financial reserves for the Town. Appropriations to such fund remain in the stabilization fund from year to year until appropriated by a two-thirds vote of Town Meeting for any legal purpose. Appropriation of monies into this fund requires a majority vote of Town Meeting. This article transfers funds to the general purpose "rainy day fund.” Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 7-0 Reasoning: In Favor: Consistent with sound financial management, the Town is placing currently available Free Cash into a designated fund for future use. The amount is equal to the amount withdrawn from the Fund at last year’s Town Meeting when less Free Cash was available for use. Opposed: Some or all of these funds could be used to fund current needs. Discussion if the General Stabilization Fund is the optimal reserve fund for future needs.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 52 - Free Cash to Offset the Tax Rate
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 52nd Article Name: Free Cash to Offset the Tax Rate Finance Committee Liaison: Michael Koniares Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Town Adminstrator Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to transfer and appropriate from Free Cash the sum of $335,000 to reduce the tax levy for Fiscal Year 2027. Description of Warrant: This annual article proposes to appropriate Free Cash, not otherwise used by the Town during the Annual or Special Town Meeting, if any, to reduce the tax rate for the upcoming fiscal year. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 7-0 Reasoning: In Favor: Consistent with the Town’s historical practice, these funds will be used to offset the tax levy, reducing the overall burden on taxpayers. Opposed: Some or all of these funds could be used for one-time capital purchases or obligations consistent with the general use of Free Cash.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 36 - Amend Zoning Bylaw Change Article iv 4.06 Accessory Buildings
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 36th Article Name: Amend Zoning Bylaw: Change Article IV, 4.06 Accessory Buildings Finance Committee Liaison: Heidi Fox Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Planning Board Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town take no action. Description of Warrant: THIS IS PART OF CONSENT AGENDA FOUR The Zoning Bylaw Article I definition of an Accessory Building (1.02) was added to the Zoning Bylaws at the 2025 ATM as “A detached structure including, but not limited to, a garage, greenhouse, shed, barn, pool house, or other structure not designed or suitable for human habitation.” The Dimensional and Density Regulations Article IV, 4.06 was also amended at 2025 ATM to clarify setback requirements for Accessory Buildings. This article addresses the Building Inspector’s request for clarity regarding maximum size for accessory buildings and the requirements for fences surrounding swimming pools in order to comply with MA pool safety regulations. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: NO ACTION Yes 6 No 1 Abstain 0 Reasoning: In Favor: There was concern that there might be unintended limitations on a property owner’s rights to build a permitted accessory structure because of the size limitations. For example, a property owner with 1,900 sq ft home on a large lot, that meets all setback requirements, might not be able to build a detached 700 sq ft garage with a loft because its square footage would exceed 50% of the principal structure’s square footage. (This is not to be confused with an ADU type of building.) Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Opposed: The Planning Board was responding to the Building Inspector’s request for clarity on whether a structure’s size, in relation to the principal structure, should be considered before issuing a permit. Existing structures permitted prior to this amendment would not be impacted. A property owner whose permit is denied because of the new maximum size may appeal to the ZBA.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 34 - Amend Zoning Bylaw Modify Restaurant J Full Service to Include Carry Out
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 34th Article Name: Amend Zoning Bylaw: Modify Article 1 Section 1.91 Definitions – Restaurant, Full Service to Include Carryout Service Finance Committee Liaison: Heidi Fox Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Planning Board Warrant Motion: Recommended the Town vote to amend the Topsfield Zoning Bylaw, Article I Definitions Section 1.91, as set forth in this Article ThirtyFourth in the warrant. Description of Warrant: THIS IS PART OF CONSENT AGENDA FOUR This article expands the definition to allow such establishments to offer carry-out, or full meals “to go.” Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: Choose an item. Yes No Abstain Reasoning: In Favor: Opposed: Recommendation Pending. The Planning Board will hold a public hearing on 4/15/26 and vote after the warrant goes to print.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 11 - Biennial GASB 74 and 75 Actuary Study
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: 11th Article Name: Biennial GASB 74 & 75 Actuary Study Finance Committee Liaison: Michael Koniares Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Town Treasurer Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to transfer and appropriate from Free Cash the sum of $9,000 to be expended by the Select Board to fund the biennial GASB 74 & 75 Actuary Study, including all incidental and related expenses. Description of Warrant: This article would provide funds for the Town’s Treasurer and Collector’s Department to contract a required third-party financial consultant to provide a biennial government accounting standards board (“GASB”) actuary study of the Town’s Other PostEmployment Benefits (OPEB) liability as required by law. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 7-0 Reasoning: In Favor: This actuary study is required by law and is conducted every other year to inform the Town’s OPEB liabilities. Opposed: This expense could alternatively be included in the Treasurer’s operating budget instead of using Free Cash.

title: FY2027 Warrant Article 20 - Fire Compressor and Cylinder Fill Station
text: Finance Committee FY2027 Warrant Vote Details Article Number: Article Name: 20 Fire Compressor and Cylinder Fill Station Finance Committee Liaison: Michael Hartman Warrant Dept/Sponsor: Fire Department. Warrant Motion: Recommended that the Town vote to transfer and appropriate from Free Cash the sum of $75,000 to be expended by the Select Board, with the advice of the Fire Chief, to purchase and install a new Fire Compressor and Cylinder Fill Station, including all incidental and related expenses. Description of Warrant: This is an air compressor system that consists of and air compressor plus large storage tanks that provide compressed air for fire fighter air tanks (4100 psi) as well as a source of compressed air for other fire department uses. Existing system is 30 years old. Finance Committee Recommendation: Finance Committee Vote: POSITIVE ACTION 7-0 Reasoning: In Favor: A functioning compressor tank is needed for the safety of the fire fighters. Opposed: No opposition.

text: TOWN OF TOPSFIELD MASSACHUSETTS Special Town Meeting Warrant TOWN MEETING TUESDAY, JUNE 16, 2026 Masconomet Regional School High School Auditorium 20 Endicott Road Boxford, MA Topsfield FY2027 letter from the Finance Committee May 27, 2026 Dear Fellow Residents, The FY2027 budget process has proven to be exceptionally challenging, forcing the citizens of Topsfield to make difficult decisions. It is important, now more than ever, for residents to actively participate in town government through attending meetings and voting, to ensure all voices are heard and considered as tradeoffs are being proposed that will shape Topsfield for years to come. Current Situation e At Town Meeting on May 5" a town budget was approved that was contingent on the passing of two overrides © To support the costs of the town’s operations © Topsfield’s share of both the Masco and Essex Tech budgets e At the Town Election on May 7" both of these overrides failed e Boxford and Middleton subsequently voted to approve the Masco budget at their respective Town Meetings, obligating Topsfield to pay its portion without adjustment ¢ The Essex Tech School District voted to approve the Essex Tech budget, obligating Topsfield to pay its portion without adjustment Next Steps Due to the differing results between Town Meeting and the Election, the Town does not currently have an approved budget for FY2027, necessitating both another Town Meeting and election. Overview of the Challenge Massachusetts Proposition 2 % serves as a check on municipal tax increases by requiring citizen approval, through an election, for increases to the tax levy above 2.5%. The cost of running the Town with its current level of service is increasing significantly above 2.5% per year with budget line examples such as health insurance and pensions increasing 12.9% and 7.7% this year respectively. This creates a structural deficit where it is mathematically impossible to balance the Town’s budget within the confines of Proposition 2 % while maintaining the same level of service. Available Options The Town has four levers with which to shape the impact of the budget on taxpayers. The only levers remaining for consideration at this point in the process are #3 and #4: Topsfield FY2027 letter from the Finance Committee May 27, 2026 Example Impact on FY27 1. Increase Revenue Encourage responsible Not available; Requires long-term development planning Largely not available; Years of “belt tightening” to avoid town overrides has 2. Cost Saving Efficiencies Deliver same level of | resulted in a very tight budget; Serious service at lower cost changes would require long-term planning and should be considered for FY28 3. Increase Taxes Overrides Available Town hall, Library, Schools, Public Safety Available 4. Reduce Services New Budget Proposal The revised budget for consideration totals $28,454,186, which is $137,000 lower than what was previously approved at the May 5 Town Meeting. The $137,000 reduction is driven by the following items: e The removal of two requested positions in the Fire Department and Planning Department e Reduction in assumptions of utilization of employee benefits This proposed budget will be balanced based on the results of the three overrides on the election ballot: $ Impact to Ballot Question Amount Average Significant Impacts if NOT Passed Taxpayer (est) 1. General Operatin: e Elementary budget Budget ° . $123,000 $54 ¢ Cuts to Road, Bridge, and Sidewalk repairs e Recreation Department 2. Masco $140,316 $62 ¢ Composting drop-off ¢ Police Community Initiatives e Library staffing 3. Essex Tech $93,472 $41 e Field Maintenance e Public Safety part time staffing Topsfield FY2027 letter from the Finance Committee May 27, 2026 Fundamental Question to Voters It is the role of the Town Administrator, Select Board, and Finance Committee to present Topstfield’s citizens with options and recommendations, and explanations of the impact of both. It is the role of the citizens to decide if they prefer to support overrides to meet the rising costs of delivering the current services provided by the Town, or reduce spending by offering fewer services. Looking Ahead It is the expectation of the Finance Committee that municipalities across Massachusetts will continue to face budget challenges for years to come. It is with this view that the Finance Committee advocates for thoughtful decisions around trade-offs and the avoidance of “quick-fixes” that will increase the budget challenges of future years. It should also be understood, given the expectation of future challenges, that reductions in services made for FY27 should be assumed permanent for the foreseeable future. The Finance Committee would like to thank all the citizens and Town employees who have been active participants in the budgeting process. Many have sacrificed sleep and time with family to ensure the best outcome for our town. Respectfully submitted by the Topsfield Finance Committee, Che Elwell, Chair Catherine Hodges, Vice Chair Michael Hartmann Heidi Fox Michael Koniares David Larson Thomas Watkins TOWN OF TOPSFIELD WARRANT FOR 2026 SPECIAL TOWN MEETING Essex, ss. To the Constable of the Town of Topsfield, in said County, In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are directed to notify the inhabitants of the Town of Topsfield, qualified to vote in elections and in Town affairs, to meet at the MASCONOMET REGIONAL SCHOOL HIGH SCHOOL AUDITORIUM 20 ENDICOTT ROAD BOXFORD MA in Boxford, on Tuesday, the sixteenth day of June, 2026, at seven o’clock in the evening (7:00 PM) then and there to act on the following articles: ARTICLE FIRST: REPORTS To hear all reports that may legally come before the meeting. ARTICLE SECOND: GENERAL OPERATING BUDGET To see if the Town will vote to fix the annual salary and compensation of all elected officers, and raise and assess, or transfer from available funds, and appropriate a sum of money for elementary schools, highways, public safety and other Town expenses from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, for Fiscal Year 2027, and determine the manner of expending the same; and to make appropriate adjustments to the votes taken under Articles Third, Fifth and Sixth of the May 5, 2026 Annual Town Meeting, or take any other action relative thereto. Recommended that the Town vote to: (1) amend the votes taken at the May 5, 2026 Annual Town Meeting under Article Fifth for the Masconomet Regional School District Fiscal Year 2027 Operating Assessment and Article Sixth for the Essex North Shore Agricultural and Technical School District Fiscal Year 2027 Gross Budget Assessment, to delete the contingencies set forth therein so that the budgets for Masconomet Regional School District and Essex North Shore Agricultural and Technical School District are fully funded regardless of whether the related overrides are approved; Page 1 of 4
